articles.title: Ruzaltatug rezetecan versus chemotherapy for EGFR-mutated advanced non-small-cell lung cancer progressing after EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor therapy (HERON-Lung01): interim analysis of a randomised, open-label, phase 3 trial in China.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Ruzaltatug rezetecan is a novel HER3-directed antibody-drug conjugate that has shown promising antitumour activity and manageable safety in pretreated EGFR-.mutated non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) in a phase 1 trial. We aimed to compare the efficacy and safety of ruzaltatug rezetecan with chemotherapy in patients with EGFR-mutated advanced NSCLC that had progressed after EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) therapy. METHODS: HERON-Lung01 is a randomised, open-label, phase 3 trial conducted at 62 sites in China. Eligible patients were aged 18-75 years, with locally advanced or metastatic non-squamous NSCLC harbouring an EGFR activating mutation (exon 19 deletion or L858R mutation), and had progressed during or after EGFR-TKI therapy. Patients were randomly assigned (1:1) to receive ruzaltatug rezetecan 8·0 mg/kg or chemotherapy comprising pemetrexed 500 mg/m FINDINGS: Between Nov 29, 2024, and Jan 29, 2026, 498 patients were randomly assigned to receive ruzaltatug rezetecan (n=250) or chemotherapy (n=248). The median age was 60·0 years (IQR 54·0-68·0); 276 (55%) patients were female and 222 (45%) male. At the prespecified interim PFS analysis, median follow-up was 7·7 months (95% CI 7·1-8·3). BICR-assessed PFS was significantly longer with ruzaltatug rezetecan than with chemotherapy (median 8·3 months vs 5·4 months; hazard ratio 0·47 [95% CI 0·36-0·60]; one-sided p<0·0001). Grade 3 or worse treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs) occurred in 101 (41%) of 248 patients receiving ruzaltatug rezetecan and 93 (39%) of 239 patients receiving chemotherapy, most commonly decreased neutrophil count (64 [26%] of 248 patients vs 46 [19%] of 239 patients), decreased white blood cell count (29 [12%] vs 29 [12%]), and anaemia (15 [6%] vs 26 [11%]). TRAEs led to treatment discontinuation in three (1%) patients in the ruzaltatug rezetecan group and three (1%) in the chemotherapy group. One death (unknown cause) in the ruzaltatug rezetecan group was considered by the investigator to be possibly treatment related. INTERPRETATION: Ruzaltatug rezetecan significantly prolonged PFS compared with chemotherapy, with a manageable safety profile, in EGFR-TKI-resistant, EGFR-mutated advanced NSCLC. These data support ruzaltatug rezetecan as a potential treatment option in this setting. FUNDING: Jiangsu Hengrui Pharmaceuticals.

articles.title: Spatial Organization of Tumor-Infiltrating B Cells Informs Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor Response in Claudin 18.2-Expressing Gastric Cancer.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Claudin 18.2 (CLDN18.2), a tight junction protein normally expressed in the gastric epithelium and rendered accessible during malignant transformation, has emerged as a key therapeutic target. Here, we seek to characterize the immune microenvironment of CLDN18.2-expressing gastric cancer and identify immune features associated with CLDN18.2 expression status. EXPERIMENTAL DESIGN: Tumor-immune features were profiled in 103 patients with HER2-neg/low advanced gastric cancer treated with first-line immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) using multiplex immunohistochemistry [7,423,483 cells across 2,315 regions of interest (ROI)]. The findings were validated in five published whole-transcriptome sequencing/microarray cohorts (1,521 samples), including the landmark CheckMate 649 phase III trial. Spatial immune architecture was assessed by cellular neighborhood analysis. Digital spatial profiling (DSP) was performed on 480 ROIs from a CLDN18.2-annotated tissue microarray (75 patients). RESULTS: CLDN18.2high tumors showed reproducible enrichment of humoral pathways, with higher CD20+ B-cell density and enrichment of B-cell/plasma-cell signatures. CLDN18.2 status alone was not associated with response or survival on first-line ICI therapy; in CLDN18.2low tumors, B-cell enrichment was associated with ICI benefit, unlike CLDN18.2high tumors. Spatial analyses indicated that CLDN18.2high tumors preferentially harbored tumor-infiltrating B cells, rather than tertiary lymphoid structure/lymphoid aggregate-like neighborhoods, and this tumor-compartment localization was associated with diminished ICI benefit. DSP confirmed that CD20+ B-cell enrichment was most pronounced within tumor regions, alongside compartment-specific activation of humoral and extrafollicular response programs and interferon-associated and remodeling signatures. CONCLUSIONS: CLDN18.2high gastric cancer exhibits a humoral-enriched microenvironment with increased tumor-infiltrating B cells and spatial immune organization associated with reduced ICI benefit. Spatial and humoral-state biomarkers may inform ongoing CLDN18.2-directed combination trials.

articles.title: Combining quizartinib with intensive chemotherapy for older patients with newly diagnosed AML: results of the UK NCRI AML18 trial.
articles.abstract: We assessed the addition of the tyrosine kinase inhibitor quizartinib, following intensive chemotherapy and as maintenance, for patients aged >60 years with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) or high-risk myelodysplastic syndrome, regardless of FLT3 mutation status. Four hundred sixty three patients (median age, 68 years) were randomized (1:1) to receive quizartinib 40 mg or not for 14 days immediately following chemotherapy courses 2 and 3, plus 28 additional days; those allocated quizartinib were further randomized (1:1) to either 12 additional 28-day maintenance courses ("long quizartinib") or no further treatment ("short quizartinib"). Median follow-up was 76 months. Three hundred fourteen patients were FLT3-wild-type (WT); 116 had FLT3 mutations. The primary end point, overall survival (OS) unselected by FLT3 status, showed no significant benefit, and there was a significant increase in non-relapse mortality with quizartinib. In a pre-planned subgroup analysis, patients with FLT3 mutations who received quizartinib had significantly improved OS (Hazard Ratio, 0.59; 95% Confidence Interval, 0.37-0.93; P = .024) due to reduced relapse risk, with greater benefit in the short quizartinib group. In patients with FLT3-WT, there was no survival benefit and no reduction in relapse risk. No significant differences were observed in time to hematologic count recovery or in length of hospitalization. The most observed grade 3/4 adverse events were febrile neutropenia. In conclusion, the addition of quizartinib to intensive chemotherapy, delayed until chemotherapy course 2, prolonged OS in older patients with FLT3-mutated AML but did not improve OS in non-FLT3-selected patients. This trial was registered at www.isrctn.com as ISRCTN-31682779 and at www.clinicaltrialsregister.eu as EudraCR-2013-002730-21.

articles.title: [Articles] Iberdomide plus daratumumab and dexamethasone versus daratumumab, bortezomib, and dexamethasone in patients with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma (EXCALIBER-RRMM): an open-label, randomised, controlled, phase 3 trial
articles.abstract: Iberdomide, daratumumab, and dexamethasone significantly improved MRD-negative complete response compared with daratumumab, bortezomib, and dexamethasone. The most common grade 3 or grade 4 adverse events were haematological events and infections, which were mostly manageable with standard supportive care. These findings support iberdomide, daratumumab, and dexamethasone as an efficacious treatment option for patients with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma with the potential to be administered across diverse care settings.

articles.title: [Articles] Neoadjuvant short-course radiotherapy followed by camrelizumab and chemotherapy versus standard of care for locally advanced rectal cancer (UNION): a prespecified interim analysis of a multicentre, open-label, randomised, phase 3 trial
articles.abstract: In this interim analysis, short-course radiotherapy followed by camrelizumab and CAPOX significantly improved 3-year event-free survival in patients with locally advanced rectal cancer, with a safety profile similar to long-course chemoradiotherapy followed by CAPOX. Comparison of this promising new treatment strategy with contemporary total neoadjuvant therapy strategies is warranted.

articles.title: Extended Follow-up of Botensilimab plus Balstilimab in an Expanded Cohort of Microsatellite-Stable Metastatic Colorectal Cancer without Active Liver Metastases.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Microsatellite-stable metastatic colorectal cancer (MSS mCRC) has limited treatment options and responds poorly to conventional immunotherapy. We report extended follow-up results from a fully enrolled, phase Ib cohort evaluating botensilimab [BOT; Fc-enhanced anti-cytotoxic T-lymphocyte-associated protein 4 (CTLA-4)] plus balstilimab [BAL; anti-programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1)] in patients with MSS mCRC and no active liver metastases (NLM). PATIENTS AND METHODS: Patients received BOT 1 or 2 mg/kg every 6 weeks plus BAL 3 mg/kg every 2 weeks up to 2 years or until progression or unacceptable toxicity. The primary objective was safety/tolerability. Efficacy endpoints included objective response rate (ORR), duration of response (DOR), and progression-free survival (PFS); overall survival (OS) was exploratory. Patients with prior regorafenib, trifluridine/tipiracil ± bevacizumab, or fruquintinib ("late-line exposed") were analyzed post hoc. RESULTS: As of December 13, 2025, 123 patients were treated [median follow-up, 20.2 months (range, 0.7-62.3)]. The median prior lines was 3 (range, 1-10; 67% had ≥3 prior lines). The most common treatment-related adverse events were diarrhea (39%; grade ≥3, 8%) and fatigue (37%; grade ≥3, 2%). The ORR was 21% [95% confidence interval (CI), 14-29]. The median DOR was not reached (NR; 95% CI, 7.3-NR), the median PFS was 4.0 months (95% CI, 2.8-4.1), and the median OS was 21.2 months [95% CI, 16.2-23.8; 36-month OS, 33% (95% CI, 24-43)]. Efficacy was consistent in late line-exposed patients [n = 37; ORR, 22% (95% CI, 10-38); median OS, 16.2 months (95% CI, 9.7-31.3)]. CONCLUSIONS: BOT + BAL demonstrated durable responses, long-term survival, and manageable safety in previously treated MSS mCRC NLM, including in late line-exposed patients. These results support further evaluation.

articles.title: B cell depletion improves therapeutic index of combination checkpoint blockade in patients with advanced melanoma.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUNDCombined checkpoint blockade (CCB) of programmed-death-1 (PD-1) and cytotoxic-T-lymphocyte-associated protein-4 (CTLA-4) is highly active in melanoma but limited by significant morbidity from immune-related adverse events (irAEs). Effective strategies to prevent CCB-mediated irAEs are lacking.METHODSPatients with advanced melanoma were randomly assigned to receive standard of care ipilimumab and nivolumab alone (Arm A: ipi/nivo, n = 7) or with one cycle of rituximab (Arm B; ipi/nivo+rituximab, n = 7).RESULTSPatients receiving ipi/nivo+rituximab experienced lower rates of greater than grade-3(G3) irAEs (14% versus 57%) and superior G3-irAE-free survival compared with those in ipi/nivo arm (2-year G3-irAE-free survival 86% versus 29%, P = 0.01), without adverse impact on tumor regression or survival. G3 hypersensitivity reactions to rituximab (43% in Arm B) prompted trial closure. Rituximab depleted pretherapy activated naive B cells linked to autoimmunity and enhanced CCB-mediated induction of myeloid inflammation and CXCL13+ICOS+ CD4 T cells.CONCLUSIONB cell depletion favorably modulates CCB-mediated immune activation and may reduce irAE risk.TRIAL REGISTRATIONClinicalTrials.gov NCT03719131.FUNDINGNIH CA238471, AR077926, CA289978, and CA290302.

articles.title: A Phase II Trial of Pembrolizumab plus Granulocyte-Macrophage Colony-Stimulating Factor in Advanced Biliary Cancer.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICI) have limited activity as monotherapy in biliary cancers. Granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor (GM-CSF) is a pleiotropic immune cell growth factor that achieved prolonged survival when combined with ipilimumab in melanoma. We conducted a single-center, phase II trial to evaluate the efficacy and safety of combining GM-CSF with pembrolizumab in patients with advanced biliary cancers after prior chemotherapy but no prior ICI. PATIENTS AND METHODS: Pembrolizumab 200 mg was administered intravenously in 21-day cycles, along with two cycles of GM-CSF 250 μg subcutaneously on days 1 through 14. The primary endpoint was the objective response rate (ORR). RESULTS: Among 42 patients enrolled, the median age was 61 years; 67% had intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma, 90% had stage IV disease, and 24% had underlying viral hepatitis. The confirmed ORR was 12% (95% confidence interval, 4-26), including two patients with a complete response, and 26% of patients had progression-free survival (PFS) ongoing at 6 months. Treatment was well tolerated, with treatment-related grade 3 to 4 events in 7% and treatment-related serious adverse events in 10%. Tumor programmed cell death ligand 1 expression was present in 46% and was associated with a higher rate of 6-month PFS. Paired tumor biopsies showed upregulation of CD8+ T-cell populations and antigen processing pathways after the addition of GM-CSF. CONCLUSIONS: The addition of GM-CSF to pembrolizumab was well tolerated but did not meet the prespecified response rate for efficacy. A subset of patients experienced deep responses and prolonged stable disease. GM-CSF elicited changes in the tumor immune microenvironment that could guide future combination approaches.

articles.title: Multikinase Inhibition with Tinengotinib in Advanced Solid Tumors: Results from a Multicenter Phase Ib/II Trial.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Tinengotinib, a multikinase inhibitor targeting Aurora kinases A/B, fibroblast growth factor receptors (FGFRs) 1 to 3, vascular endothelial growth factor receptor 2, and Janus kinases 1 to 2, was evaluated in this phase Ib/II study to assess safety, pharmacokinetics (PK), efficacy, and genomic correlates of response and resistance in patients with advanced solid tumors. PATIENTS AND METHODS: Patients with advanced/metastatic solid tumors lacking standard treatment options were enrolled at 7 sites in the United States (NCT04742959). Tinengotinib was administered at 12 mg once daily in arm A and at multiple dose levels/dosing schedules in arm C. RESULTS: Among 197 patients receiving tinengotinib, treatment-related treatment-emergent adverse events occurred in 160 (81.2%) patients, with hypertension being the most common. Hyperphosphatemia and ocular toxicities were uncommon. Clinical benefit was achieved by 43 of 159 (27.0%) evaluable patients, including 1 complete response, 20 partial responses, and 22 stable diseases ≥6 months. Antitumor activity was most pronounced with 10-mg and 12-mg dose levels. The objective response rates were 33.3%, 30%, and 13% in prostate cancer (n = 15), breast cancer (n = 20), and cholangiocarcinoma (n = 23), respectively. PK analyses supported the 10-mg once-daily regimen. Exploratory genomic analyses identified potential molecular correlations of response, including FGFR2 fusions in cholangiocarcinoma responders. Additional observations in breast cancer, including ROS1 alterations, were exploratory and should be considered hypothesis generating. Exploratory analyses also suggested associations between EGFR or MLL mutations in cholangiocarcinoma and MYC alterations in prostate cancer with shorter progression-free survival, consistent with emerging evidence linking MYC-driven lineage plasticity to androgen receptor-independent disease biology. Reductions in circulating tumor DNA variant allele frequency further supported pharmacodynamic target engagement. CONCLUSIONS: Tinengotinib demonstrated manageable toxicity with antitumor activity across advanced solid tumors, with infrequent hyperphosphatemia and ocular toxicities. Integrated PK-biomarker analyses support the continued clinical development of tinengotinib and the exploration of biomarker-informed precision oncology strategies.

articles.title: Danvatirsen plus Pembrolizumab versus Pembrolizumab for Recurrent and/or Metastatic Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma (PEMDA-HN): A Randomized, Phase II Trial.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Signal transducer and activator of transcription 3 (STAT3) is important in promoting a pro-oncogenic tumor microenvironment. This first randomized trial of a STAT3-targeting antisense oligonucleotide with pembrolizumab assessed whether this first-line combination would improve outcomes compared with pembrolizumab alone in recurrent/metastatic (R/M) head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC). PATIENTS AND METHODS: This multicenter, randomized, open-label, controlled study (NCT05814666) enrolled patients with previously untreated R/M HNSCC with positive PD-L1 expression [combined positive score (CPS) ≥1]. Patients were stratified by CPS (1-19; ≥20) and randomized 2:1 to danvatirsen 3 mg/kg intravenously weekly (with two loading doses in week 1) plus pembrolizumab 200 mg intravenously every 3 weeks or pembrolizumab alone. Patients received 21-day treatment cycles until progressive disease, unacceptable toxicity, or voluntary withdrawal. Primary endpoint was overall response rate (ORR; partial + complete response per RECIST v1.1). RESULTS: Sixty-nine patients were randomized, and 66 were treated [51 (77.3%) male]: 45 with danvatirsen + pembrolizumab and 21 with pembrolizumab alone. Enrollment was stopped due to lack of response in the CPS 1 to 19 cohort after ≥1 scan (∼6 weeks of treatment) and in the CPS ≥20 cohort after ≥2 scans (∼12 weeks). In the final analysis, ORRs were 15.6% and 14.3%, respectively (risk difference 1.3; P = 1). The treatment-emergent adverse event rate was increased in the combination arm (97.8% vs. 85.7%), and the combination side effect profile was similar to previous danvatirsen studies. CONCLUSIONS: Combination danvatirsen + pembrolizumab did not improve ORR compared with pembrolizumab alone in first-line treatment of R/M HNSCC. Further exploration of STAT3-targeted approaches is needed within the context of immunotherapy.

articles.title: EMB-01, an Anti-EGFR/c-MET Bispecific Antibody, in Patients with Heavily Pretreated Metastatic Colorectal Cancer from a Phase Ib/II, Open-Label, Multicenter Study.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: EMB-01 is a novel epidermal growth factor receptor × mesenchymal-epithelial transition factor bispecific antibody. The phase Ib/II study (NCT05176665) presents the safety and antitumor activity of EMB-01 in patients predominantly with heavily pretreated metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC). PATIENTS AND METHODS: EMB-01 was administered at 1,600 mg intravenously weekly. Primary endpoints were safety and tolerability in phase Ib and antitumor activity in phase II. Secondary endpoints included cross-phase validation of antitumor activity and safety. Exploratory endpoints included biomarker analysis. RESULTS: Fifty-two patients were enrolled (phase Ib, n = 27; phase II, n = 25). All patients (100%) experienced at least one treatment-emergent adverse event, and 98.1% experienced treatment-related adverse events (TRAE). Grade ≥3 TRAEs occurred in 63.5% of patients, with rash (25%) and dermatitis acneiform (17.3%) most frequently. Among the 48 patients with mCRC, the confirmed objective response rate (cORR) was 12.5% [95% confidence interval (CI), 4.7%-25.2%], with a median duration of response of 32 weeks (95% CI, 16-not estimable). All responses were observed in a favorable mCRC subgroup with evaluable response [left-sided, RAS/RAF wild-type, naïve to fruquintinib/regorafenib/trifluridine-tipiracil (TAS-102); n = 29]. In this subgroup, the unconfirmed ORR (uORR) and the cORR were 24.1% (95% CI, 10.3%-43.5%) and 20.7% (95% CI, 8%-39.7%), respectively. Median progression-free survival was 19 weeks (95% CI, 12.3-24.1 weeks). CONCLUSIONS: EMB-01 demonstrated a manageable safety profile and promising antitumor activity in heavily pretreated mCRC, particularly in the RAS/RAF wild-type, left-sided mCRC subgroup naïve to late-line therapies, warranting further clinical development.

articles.title: Dual Inhibition of LAG-3 and PD-1 with IBI110 and Sintilimab in Advanced Alveolar Soft Part Sarcoma: A Single-Center, Phase II Trial.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Alveolar soft part sarcoma (ASPS) is an ultrarare soft tissue sarcoma. Current standard therapy with PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors achieves limited response rates (<40%). Lymphocyte-activation gene 3 (LAG-3) is coexpressed with PD-1 on exhausted T cells, and dual blockade has shown synergy in some solid tumors but remains unexplored in sarcoma. This trial evaluated the efficacy of IBI110 (anti-LAG-3) plus sintilimab (anti-PD-1) in advanced ASPS. PATIENTS AND METHODS: This open-label, phase II study enrolled 28 patients from July 2022 to September 2023 (median follow-up, 33.6 months). Both drugs were given intravenously at 200 mg every 3 weeks. The primary endpoint was overall response rate (ORR) by RECIST v1.1. RESULTS: Among 28 patients, 8 (28.6%) were resistant to prior immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICI), and 20 (71.4%) were ICI-naïve. The overall ORR was 51.8% (14/27 evaluable), including 4 complete responses and 10 partial responses. During a median follow-up of 33.6 months, the median progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS) were not reached in the whole population. In ICI-naïve patients, the ORR was 60%, with median PFS/OS not reached. In ICI-resistant patients, the ORR was 25%, with median PFS of 14.9 months and median OS of 25.4 months. The median time to response was 3.3 months; the median duration of response (DoR) was not reached. Grade 3 to 4 treatment-related adverse events occurred in nine patients (32.1%), with no treatment-related deaths. Exploratory analysis showed that responders had significantly higher baseline LAG-3+ cell density in tumor specimens. CONCLUSIONS: Dual LAG-3/PD-1 blockade demonstrated promising and durable antitumor activity with manageable safety in both ICI-naïve and ICI-resistant advanced ASPS, warranting further investigation.

articles.title: Neoadjuvant Nivolumab plus Carboplatin and Paclitaxel in Patients with Locally Advanced Resectable Squamous Cell Carcinoma of the Head and Neck: A Phase II, Single-Arm Trial.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: In locally advanced resectable squamous cell carcinoma of the head and neck (SCCHN), patients treated with neoadjuvant chemotherapy with major pathologic response (MPR) or pathologic complete response (pCR) have overall survival (OS) rates superior to those of patients with poorer pathologic responses. To improve efficacy, we added the PD-1 inhibitor nivolumab to neoadjuvant chemotherapy and evaluated the combination. PATIENTS AND METHODS: In this single-arm, open-label phase II trial, patients with newly diagnosed stage III to IV human papillomavirus (HPV)-negative SCCHN in the oral cavity, oropharynx, hypopharynx, and larynx or stage II to III HPV-positive oropharyngeal SCCHN received neoadjuvant carboplatin and paclitaxel (6 weeks) plus nivolumab (every other week), followed by surgery and adjuvant radiotherapy ± chemotherapy. The primary endpoint was pCR at the primary site. RESULTS: Thirty-four patients were enrolled and received neoadjuvant therapy. Thirty-three patients received surgery (R0 resection = 100%). Disease sites included the oral cavity (79%), oropharynx (12%), hypopharynx (6%), and larynx (3%). Twenty-eight (85%) patients had stage IVA disease. The median postsurgical follow-up was 35.3 months. Fourteen (41%) patients had grade 3/4 treatment-related adverse events. Twenty-seven (82%) patients completed all cycles of neoadjuvant therapy. Twenty-four (73%) patients had at least an MPR at the primary site, and 15 (45%) had a pCR. In an unplanned analysis at 3 years, recurrence-free survival and OS were 74% and 83%, respectively. CONCLUSIONS: This phase II trial of neoadjuvant nivolumab plus carboplatin and paclitaxel in previously untreated, locally advanced, resectable SCCHN was well tolerated and reached its primary endpoint of pCR at the primary site. A phase III confirmatory study is warranted in advanced-stage, resectable HPV-negative SCCHN. See related commentary by Anderson and Sikora, p. 4763.

articles.title: Changes in Alcohol Use among Adults with Cancer Participating in the ECOG-ACRIN EAQ171CD Tobacco Treatment Trial.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Alcohol and tobacco use are known carcinogens. Treating alcohol and tobacco co-use can improve treatment and survivorship outcomes among patients diagnosed with cancer. METHODS: We conducted a post hoc analysis of ECOG-ACRIN EAQ171CD trial participants within the National Cancer Institute (NCI) Community Oncology Research Program (NCORP), examining changes in alcohol use among adults receiving the virtual sustained treatment (VST) for tobacco use intervention versus enhanced usual care (EUC; Quitline referral). Multivariable logistic regression assessed changes in alcohol use disorder (AUD) risk at 3 and 6 months using the Alcohol Use Disorders Identification Test Concise (AUDIT-C). RESULTS: At baseline, participants (N = 305) were classified as having no risk (31%), low/minimal risk (38%), moderate risk (23%), or high risk (8%) for AUD. The mean age was 55.6 years, participants smoked for an average of 33 years, and 18% had alcohol-associated tumors. Participants randomized to EUC were more likely to shift to a lower alcohol risk category than those in the VST arm at 3 months (39% vs. 27%) and 6 months (33% vs. 27%). There was no significant difference in the odds of shifting to a lower risk category for VST versus EUC at 3 months [adjusted odds ratio (OR), 0.56; 95% confidence interval (CI), 0.26-1.18; P = 0.125] or at 6 months (adjusted OR, 0.57; 95% CI, 0.25-1.28; P = 0.172). CONCLUSIONS: Patients diagnosed with cancer and engaging in alcohol and tobacco co-use can achieve reductions in alcohol use and risk. IMPACT: Integrating tailored, co-use-focused strategies into cessation programs may improve changes in modifiable risk behaviors.

articles.title: Coronary artery calcification is not associated with survival in advanced gastric and gastroesophageal junction cancer: a secondary analysis of the EXPAND trial.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Computed tomography (CT) is the clinical standard for staging of gastrointestinal cancer. Previous studies have highlighted the prognostic significance of coronary artery calcification (CAC) detected by CT in various types of cancer. However, the prognostic role of CAC scoring in gastrointestinal cancers is still unclear. The aim of this study was to investigate the impact of CT-defined CAC on overall survival (OS) in patients with advanced gastric or gastroesophageal junction cancer. METHODS: CAC was semiquantitatively measured using the visual Weston method on baseline CT scans in 785 patients with unresectable locally advanced or metastatic gastric or gastroesophageal junction cancer from the phase III EXPAND trial. This present study is a secondary analysis of the base line CT images. In the original analysis patients were randomly assigned to first-line treatment with cisplatin/capecitabin ± cetuximab. The primary endpoint of the current subanalysis is the OS. For statistical analysis group differences were calculated using the Mann-Whitney-U test and ANOVA test. Kaplan-Meier curves and multivariable Cox regression analysis were used to test the effect of CAC on mortality. RESULTS: The median CAC score was 1 (IQR 0; 3). A total of 337 patients (42.9%) had no visible CAC (CAC score 0). Male patients had statistically significant higher CAC score compared to female patients (median 1 versus 0, p < 0.0001). In univariable Cox regression CAC showed no significant association with survival when analysed as a continuous value (HR: 0.99, 95% CI: 0.96-1.02, p = 0.74), and when dichotomized for absence and presence of calcification (HR:1.08, 95% CI: 0.92-1.26, p = 0.34). Similar results were identified in further subgroup analyses. CONCLUSION: CT-defined CAC scoring has no relevant prognostic impact in advanced gastric and gastroesophageal junction cancer undergoing first-line chemotherapy. The present study cannot confirm the promising results for CAC scoring in lung cancer patients.

articles.title: Sunlight Exposure and Breast Cancer Risk: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Sunlight exposure may influence breast cancer risk through cutaneous vitamin D synthesis, circadian regulation, and immune modulation, yet prior meta-analyses were limited and did not examine hormone receptor subtypes. In this systematic review and random-effects meta-analysis of 31 epidemiologic studies, higher sunlight exposure was associated with lower breast cancer incidence [pooled odds ratio (OR), 0.80; 95% confidence interval (CI), 0.74-0.86], with the strongest associations in case-control studies using personal exposure measures and weaker associations in cohorts relying on ambient ultraviolet proxies. Protection was confined to estrogen receptor (ER)-negative (OR, 0.71; 95% CI, 0.58-0.87) and triple-negative tumors (OR, 0.55; 95% CI, 0.37-0.81), with no association for ER-positive disease, and survival was improved for diagnoses in sunnier seasons (hazard ratio, 0.84; 95% CI, 0.80-0.88), whereas a dose-response analysis indicated an 8% lower risk per 10 relative exposure units. Because the evidence is observational and subject to confounding and exposure misclassification, these hypothesis-generating findings nonetheless support further study of the light environment in breast cancer etiology and prevention, balanced against skin cancer risk.

articles.title: Sitagliptin, a repurposed diabetes drug, overcomes gemcitabine resistance in pancreatic cancer via ribonucleotide reductase inhibition: SITGEM-CARE phase 2 trial.
articles.abstract: Gemcitabine resistance remains a major therapeutic barrier in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC), for which median survival in advanced disease has remained near one year despite extensive clinical investigation. Using artificial intelligence (AI)-guided structure-based drug repurposing, we identified sitagliptin, a DPP-4 inhibitor for diabetes, as a candidate ribonucleotide reductase (RRM1/2) inhibitor that sensitizes PDAC to gemcitabine. Molecular dynamics simulations suggested that sitagliptin disrupts gemcitabine-RRM1/2 interactions, downregulating RRM1/2 expression and restoring chemosensitivity across PDAC cell lines, patient-derived organoids, and mouse models. Sitagliptin enhanced the anti-tumor efficacy of both gemcitabine-nab-paclitaxel (GnP) and FOLFIRINOX regimens in preclinical studies. We conducted SITGEM-CARE, a single-center phase 2 trial in 22 patients with locally advanced or metastatic PDAC (median age 65.0 years; ECOG performance status 1, 86.4%; Stage IV, 68.2%; liver metastases, 54.5%). Patients received sitagliptin 100 mg orally once daily continuously, plus gemcitabine 1000 mg/m² and nab-paclitaxel 125 mg/m² on days 1 and 8 of 21-day cycles. Among 22 evaluable patients, eight achieved a partial response, and 11 had stable disease, yielding an objective response rate of 36.4% (95% CI: 17.2-59.3%) and a disease control rate of 86.4% (95% CI: 65.1-97.1%), with tumor shrinkage in 86.4% of patients. At a median follow-up of 9.9 months, the median progression-free survival was 6.6 months (95% CI: 4.8-12.4) with 6-month and 9-month PFS rates of 63.6% and 43.5%, respectively. Median overall survival was 12.5 months (95% CI: 7.8-not reached), with 62.9% of patients alive at 12 months. Furthermore, treatment was well tolerated, with no Grade 4/5 treatment-related adverse events. These findings are hypothesis-generating and warrant confirmation in adequately powered, randomized trials. ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT05947825.

articles.title: CAR-NK Cells in B-cell Lymphoma: A New Frontier toward Accessible and Scalable Cellular Therapy.
articles.abstract: In this phase II study, TAK-007, an off-the-shelf allogeneic CD19 CAR NK-cell therapy expressing IL-15, demonstrates encouraging response rates, rapid treatment availability, and an excellent safety profile in heavily pretreated B-cell lymphoma, including post-CAR-T patients, albeit with limited durability. These findings, supported by integrated translational analyses, provide important mechanistic insights into CAR-NK biology that may guide future optimization and bring this approach closer to broader clinical application. See related article by Darrah et al., p. 892.

articles.title: Adjuvant mFOLFOXIRI after curative-intent resection of oligometastatic colorectal cancer: phase II FANTASTIC trial.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Patients with oligometastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC) remain at high risk of recurrence after curative surgery, yet the benefit of adjuvant chemotherapy remains inconclusive. This study evaluated the feasibility and efficacy of adjuvant modified (m)FOLFOXIRI (irinotecan, oxaliplatin, L-leucovorin (L-LV), 5-fluorouracil (5-FU)), as well as the utility of circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA) as a prognostic and predictive biomarker in mCRC. METHODS: Between October 2020 and January 2024, patients with histologically confirmed mCRC undergoing complete metastasectomy were enrolled in this multicentre non-randomized phase II study. Eligible and consenting patients received eight cycles of mFOLFOXIRI followed by four cycles of 5-FU/L-LV; ineligible/non-consenting patients received standard of care (SOC; CAPOX (capecitabine and oxaliplatin), 5-FU, or observation). ctDNA was assessed using the tumour-informed personalized Signatera™ assay (Natera, Austin, TX, USA) at 28 days and 7 months after surgery. The primary endpoint was completion of eight cycles of mFOLFOXIRI in a target sample of 36 patients. RESULTS: Of the 83 registered patients, 73 were enrolled (39 mFOLFOXIRI, 34 SOC). The mFOLFOXIRI completion rate was 74% (80% confidence interval 63% to 83%; P < 0.001). ctDNA positivity predicted significantly inferior recurrence-free survival across both the mFOLFOXIRI and SOC treatment groups at 28 days (hazard ratios (HR) 7.27 and 7.17, respectively) and 7 months (HR 3.96 and 4.38, respectively) after surgery. Multivariate analysis identified ctDNA positivity, RAS mutation, metachronous metastases, and mFOLFOXIRI as significant prognostic factors. mFOLFOXIRI improved recurrence-free survival compared with SOC in the overall population (HR 0.44; P = 0.012), with a trend towards benefit in ctDNA-positive but not ctDNA-negative patients. ctDNA clearance rates were 33% (mFOLFOXIRI) and 20% (SOC). CONCLUSIONS: This study indicates the feasibility of adjuvant mFOLFOXIRI in patients with mCRC, with an acceptable safety profile and potential clinical benefit among those with ctDNA positivity 28 days after surgery.

articles.title: Neoadjuvant concurrent or sequential anthracycline-containing chemotherapy and HER2-targeted agents for HER2-positive breast cancer: a randomized phase 2 study (METIS).
articles.abstract: The integration of anthracyclines with HER2-targeted agents in neoadjuvant therapy for HER2-positive breast cancer has been limited by cardiotoxicity concerns. This randomized phase II METIS trial (NCT04172259) assessed whether concurrent pegylated liposomal doxorubicin (PLD)-containing chemotherapy plus dual HER2 blockade (trastuzumab/pertuzumab) could improve efficacy without increasing cardiac risk. A total of 156 patients with stage II-III HER2-positive breast cancer were randomized to a PLD-based concurrent regimen or an epirubicin and cyclophosphamide (EC)-based sequential regimen. The PLD-based concurrent group achieved a higher pathological complete response (pCR) rate (67.5% vs. 48.7%; difference, 18.8%; 95% confidence interval [CI], 3.6-34.0; P = 0.033) compared with the EC-based sequential group, with greater benefit in hormone receptor-positive disease (58.7% vs. 36.7%) and stage II tumors (82.1% vs. 48.0%). After a median follow-up of 37.5 months, fewer event-free survival (EFS) events occurred in the PLD-based concurrent group (3 vs. 8), yielding a hazard ratio (HR) of 0.35 (95% CI, 0.09-1.32; P = 0.105). The estimated 3-year EFS rates were 96.0% (95% CI, 88.1-98.7) versus 90.7% (95% CI, 81.5-95.6). Achieving pCR was significantly associated with improved EFS (HR = 0.15; 95% CI, 0.03-0.71; P = 0.006). Cardiac safety was comparable, with no symptomatic cardiac dysfunction and only one grade ≥3 cardiotoxicity in the EC-based sequential group. These findings support PLD-based concurrent therapy with trastuzumab and pertuzumab as an effective and safe neoadjuvant option for high-risk HER2-positive breast cancer, warranting further evaluation in phase III trials.

articles.title: Resistance training and protein supplementation in patients with incurable gastroesophageal cancer: a randomized feasibility trial.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Cancer cachexia is associated with reduced physical performance, quality of life, and survival in patients with incurable gastroesophageal cancer. Resistance training and protein supplementation have the potential to improve these outcomes. Whether an intervention comprising resistance training and protein supplementation is feasible during treatment for incurable gastroesophageal cancer is not known. METHODS: This was an open-label, parallel-group, two-arm, randomized controlled feasibility trial. Patients with incurable gastroesophageal cancer scheduled to undergo first-line chemotherapy were randomized 2:1 to resistance training three times per week and daily protein supplementation or to control. The primary outcome, feasibility, was assessed by recruitment, retention, adherence, and harms. Secondary outcomes included body composition, physical performance, quality of life, and treatment tolerability. RESULTS: Out of 106 potentially eligible patients, 20 participants (5 female and 15 male, mean age 65) were randomized yielding a recruitment rate of 19%. 18 participants completed the trial with a retention rate of 90%. Median (25th; 75th percentile) adherence to the resistance training sessions and to the protein supplements was 63% (43; 77) and 39% (17; 76), respectively. Five participants (38%) met the minimum feasibility criteria of both interventions. No serious adverse events related to the intervention occurred. We found no between-group differences in body composition, physical performance, quality of life, or treatment tolerability. CONCLUSION: Resistance training combined with protein supplementation was not feasible during first-line chemotherapy in patients with incurable gastroesophageal cancer due to low accrual and low adherence to protein supplementation. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT05650827. Study registration date 2022-12-12.

articles.title: Long-term effects of a parenting program for advanced cancer: A randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: This study examines effects over time of a telephone-delivered 5-session manualized parenting education program for child-rearing parents with advanced cancer. Primary outcomes were parents' depressed mood and anxiety, parenting skills, parenting self-efficacy, and child behavioral-emotional adjustment. METHODS: A total of 84 child-rearing parents diagnosed with advanced, non-curable cancer were recruited from community and comprehensive cancer centers and service providers serving cancer patients. After obtaining signed informed consent and baseline questionnaires, parents were randomized to an experimental treatment group or to an alternative treatment control group. Data (3, 6, and 9 months) were obtained after baseline. Linear Mixed Models were used to compare baseline with 6- and 9-month follow-ups. Outcomes at 3 months were reported earlier. RESULTS: Of the 84 parents initially randomized, 24 participants completed all data collection time periods. Mixed model analysis showed a significant change in parenting skills over all time periods that benefited the experimental group. There was also a significant improvement in parents' self-efficacy at 6 and 9 months, which benefited the control group. SIGNIFICANCE OF RESULTS: This is the first known longitudinal study of child and parent-reported outcomes from a randomized controlled trial of a manualized cancer parenting program for parents with advanced cancer. All results should be viewed with caution given the small sample size and the loss of 71% of the participants from baseline to 9 months. Despite these limitations, Linear Mixed Models analysis showed clinically significant improvements in parenting skills over time compared to an alternative treatment control group.

articles.title: Photobiomodulation for radiotherapy-induced dysgeusia in head and neck cancer patients: a pilot randomized clinical trial.
articles.abstract: Dysgeusia is a frequent complication in patients with head and neck cancer (HNC) undergoing radiotherapy and may negatively affect nutritional status and quality of life. This pilot study evaluated the effect of photobiomodulation (PBM) on the management of radiotherapy-induced dysgeusia. Sixteen patients undergoing radiotherapy for HNC were randomly assigned to either a PBM group (n = 8) or a zinc sulfate group (n = 8). Objective taste identification tests evaluating sweet, bitter, sour, and salty tastes were performed at three time points: before radiotherapy (T0), at the 15th radiotherapy session (T1), and at the 30th radiotherapy session (T2). Salty taste was the most affected taste modality in both groups. At T2, sweet taste was correctly identified by 75.0% of patients in the zinc group and 50.0% in the PBM group. In contrast, bitter taste was preserved in 87.5% of patients in the PBM group and 75.0% in the zinc group. Sour taste was preserved in 87.5% and 62.5% of patients in the PBM and zinc groups, respectively, whereas salty taste was preserved in 50.0% and 25.0% of patients, respectively. No statistically significant differences were observed between groups at T0, T1, or T2 (all p > 0.05). Although no statistically significant differences were identified, PBM was associated with better preservation of sour, bitter, and salty taste perception, particularly after the 30th radiotherapy session. These preliminary findings suggest that PBM may represent a promising supportive strategy for the management of treatment-related dysgeusia in patients with HNC undergoing radiotherapy.

articles.title: Prophylactic dexamethasone for prevention of opioid-induced nausea and vomiting in cancer patients: a randomised controlled trial (DEX-OINV Trial).
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Opioid-induced nausea and vomiting (OINV) is a common, distressing complication when starting opioids in cancer patients, yet evidence for prophylaxis is limited, and no randomised trial has evaluated dexamethasone in this setting. We assessed whether prophylactic dexamethasone reduces nausea and vomiting following initiation of oral morphine in opioid-naïve cancer patients. METHODS: In this open-label, randomised controlled trial at a tertiary cancer centre, opioid-naïve adults initiating oral morphine were randomised 1:1 to prophylactic oral dexamethasone or no prophylaxis. Rescue antiemetics were given in both arms. The primary outcome was nausea severity on an 11-point numerical rating scale (NRS) at Days 1, 3 and 5. Secondary outcomes were vomiting episodes and rescue antiemetic use. Analyses followed the intention-to-treat principle, with multivariable logistic regression adjusting for clinical covariates. RESULTS: Of 180 patients screened, 150 were randomised (dexamethasone n = 74; control n = 76). Mean nausea severity was lower with dexamethasone at all timepoints (Day 1: 1.36 vs 2.93; Day 5: 0.74 vs 1.53; both p ≤ 0.01), with a number needed to treat of 5 on Day 1 to prevent one episode of clinically meaningful nausea (NRS ≥ 4). The benefit persisted after adjustment (Day 1 aOR 0.38, 95% CI 0.19-0.75). Vomiting episodes were significantly reduced on Day 1. No serious adverse events occurred, and no patient discontinued treatment because of an adverse event. CONCLUSION: Prophylactic dexamethasone was associated with lower nausea severity during the critical early period of oral morphine initiation and was well tolerated. Dexamethasone is a widely available and inexpensive agent that warrants confirmation in larger multicentre trials. TRIAL REGISTRATION: CTRI/2026/02/104005, prospectively registered on 16 February 2026.

articles.title: Benson relaxation technique for perioperative anxiety and depressive symptoms in patients undergoing brain tumor surgery: a clinical trial.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Patients undergoing craniotomy for brain tumors confront psychophysiological crisis. Managing perioperative distress poses a clinical paradox, as standard pharmacological sedatives are carefully restricted based on neurological status and institutional protocols to avoid masking critical postoperative neurological signs. This study investigated the efficacy of the Benson relaxation technique (BRT), a nonpharmacological mind-body intervention, on perioperative anxiety and depressive symptoms in this vulnerable population. METHODS: In this clinical trial, out of 84 patients assessed for eligibility, 74 eligible patients undergoing brain tumor resection were allocated to either the BRT intervention group (n = 37) or the control group (n = 37). The intervention group completed supervised BRT sessions (muscle relaxation, diaphragmatic breathing, and word repetition) on the evening of ICU admission, 60 min preoperatively, and 24 h postoperatively. Both groups received routine care, and anxiety and depressive symptoms were evaluated at identical time points (baseline on the evening of ICU admission prior to the intervention, 30 min preoperatively, and 24 h postoperatively). Data were analyzed using analysis of covariance (ANCOVA). RESULTS: Seventy patients completed the trial (35 per group). At 24 h postoperatively, ANCOVA adjusted for baseline scores showed that the BRT group had significantly lower anxiety scores compared to the control group, with an adjusted mean difference of - 4.16 points (95% CI, - 5.40 to - 2.93; P < 0.001). Regarding depressive symptoms, baseline scores were below the threshold for clinically significant symptoms (HADS-D < 8) in both cohorts; however, at 24 h postoperatively, the BRT group had significantly lower adjusted depressive symptom scores than the control group, with an adjusted mean difference of - 2.32 points (95% CI, - 3.51 to - 1.12; P < 0.001), indicating a preventive effect against postoperative reactive depressive symptoms. CONCLUSION: The Benson relaxation technique is a safe, feasible, and well-tolerated nurse-led mind-body strategy that effectively mitigates perioperative anxiety and reduces postoperative depressive symptoms without adverse events. These findings support integrating structured nonpharmacological modalities into neurosurgical care.

articles.title: Effects of digital stress-management interventions in breast cancer patients 18 months after intervention access.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Digital stress-management tools show promise, but their long-term impact remains unclear. In the Coping After Breast Cancer (CABC) trial, the app-based stress-management program StressProffen, with either cognitive behavioral therapy intervention (CBI) or a mindfulness-based intervention (MBI), showed no advantage over usual care after six months of access. However, benefits may emerge gradually, as users need time not only to become familiar with the content and techniques, but also to internalize, apply and automatize their use in response to real-life stressors. The a priori defined aims of the current study were to examine; 1) whether extended (18 months) access to the digital stress-management interventions CBI and MBI were associated with changes in perceived stress (stress) (primary outcome), measures of health-related quality of life, mindfulness, fatigue, coping, anxiety, depression, and sleep (secondary outcomes), 2) association between app use and changes in stress level and investigate baseline characteristics as moderators of change in stress in the intervention groups, and 3) identify predictors of change in stress among patients with breast cancer. METHODS: Of 430 patients randomized to MBI, CBI, or usual care, 76% (n = 327) completed the 18-month survey. Linear mixed-effects models were used to assess between-group differences in primary and secondary outcomes. Moderator analyses were performed to examine whether specific baseline characteristics modified the intervention effects on stress levels. Predictor analysis of change in stress was performed for the total sample. RESULTS: At 18 months, all three groups showed stable trends over time, with no significant difference between either intervention group and controls. A larger stress reduction was observed among younger participants (≤50 years) in both CBI and MBI compared to controls. Higher baseline stress levels predicted significantly larger stress reductions in the total sample, but the moderator analysis showed that the effects were only significant in the CBI group. CONCLUSION: Neither CBI nor MBI showed statistically significant improvements at 18 months compared to controls. The results however suggest that long-term access to stress management interventions may help young women with breast cancer and those with high initial stress to reduce their stress levels. articles.title: Safety and Efficacy of Intratumoral MEDI1191, an IL12 mRNA Lipid Nanoparticle, plus Intravenous Durvalumab in Patients with Advanced Solid Tumors: A First-in-Human Study.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: MEDI1191 is a lipid nanoparticle-formulated messenger RNA (mRNA) designed to induce local interleukin (IL) 12 production and intensify antitumor T-cell responses. We report dose-escalation results from a first-in-human, open-label, phase I study of intratumoral MEDI1191 plus intravenous durvalumab (NCT03946800). PATIENTS AND METHODS: Patients were ≥18 years with advanced/metastatic solid tumors and had progressed on ≥1 line of prior therapy (immunotherapy permitted). Cutaneous/subcutaneous (parts 1A and 1B) or deep-seated lesions (part 1D) were injected; patients had ≥1 noninjected lesion measurable per Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (RECIST v1.1). Target lesions were noninjected. MEDI1191 and durvalumab were given sequentially (part 1A) or concurrently (parts 1B and 1D). Primary objectives were safety and determination of maximum tolerated dose (MTD). Secondary objectives included efficacy. RESULTS: As of February 27, 2023, 61 patients were treated. Patients had a median of four prior regimens (range, 1-17); 39 (63.9%) received prior anti-programmed cell death protein 1/programmed cell death ligand 1 [PD-(L)1] immunotherapy. Treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAE) occurred in 96.7% of patients, and 41.0% experienced grade 3/4 TEAEs. There were no dose-limiting toxicities. The MTD was not reached. The objective response rate was 9.8%, including 1 confirmed complete response and 5 confirmed partial responses (PR). The duration of response was 2.7 to 22.3 months; the median was not reached. Responses occurred in injected lesions, local noninjected lesions, and distant lesions. Three of the 39 patients with prior anti-PD-(L)1 therapy had PRs. CONCLUSIONS: MEDI1191 and durvalumab were tolerated. Preliminary antitumor activity was encouraging in these heavily pretreated patients, including patients previously treated with immune checkpoint inhibitors.

articles.title: Topical Esomeprazole for the Prevention and Treatment of Radiation Dermatitis in Patients With Head and Neck Cancer: Protocol for a Phase 2 Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Radiation dermatitis (RD) is a common and clinically significant toxicity affecting the majority of patients undergoing external beam radiation therapy, particularly those treated for head and neck cancer (HNC). RD can impair quality of life, limit treatment intensity, and compromise oncologic outcomes; yet, there is no established standard-of-care for its prevention or management. Preclinical studies suggest that a topically reformulated proton pump inhibitor (PPI), esomeprazole (Dermaprazole), has antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and antifibrotic properties that may mitigate radiation-induced skin injury. OBJECTIVE: This phase 2 randomized controlled trial aims to evaluate the potential safety, feasibility, and efficacy of prophylactic topical Dermaprazole compared with standard supportive care (Aquaphor) in reducing the incidence and severity of clinically significant RD in patients with HNC receiving definitive chemoradiation. METHODS: This is a prospective, single-center, randomized controlled trial with a 2:1 allocation ratio. A total of 45 adults (≥18 y) with biopsy-confirmed head and neck malignancy planned to receive definitive chemoradiation of at least 66 Gy will be enrolled. Participants will be randomized to receive twice-daily topical Dermaprazole or Aquaphor beginning at computed tomography (CT) simulation and continuing through 2 weeks after completion of radiation therapy. The primary outcome is the rate and severity of RD, assessed weekly during treatment using the National Cancer Institute (NCI) Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE) version 5 by the treating radiation oncologist, with blinded dermatologic assessment based on standardized medical photography. Feasibility outcomes include accrual rate, treatment compliance, and questionnaire completion rates. Secondary outcomes include time to onset and healing of grade ≥2 RD, quality of life assessed using the Skindex-16 instrument, radiation dose thresholds associated with dermatitis, and changes in inflammatory biomarkers (C-reactive protein, tumor necrosis factor-α, interleukin [IL]-1β, and IL-6). More specifically, secondary outcomes will be assessed through serial CTCAE version 5 evaluations for onset and healing, Skindex16 questionnaires for quality of life, radiation dose-volume parameters for dermatitis thresholds, and serum inflammatory marker concentration measurements before, during, and after treatment. RESULTS: The study began in June 2022 and has completed enrollment. Data analysis will commence following completion of data collection, with results expected to be published by 2027. CONCLUSIONS: Should Dermaprazole demonstrate efficacy in reducing RD in patients undergoing radiation therapy, it may offer an alternative or adjunctive treatment option for the prevention and management of RD, potentially reducing treatment-related morbidity and improving patients' quality of life during radiotherapy. articles.title: [Policy Review] Reporting health-related quality of life in randomised clinical trials evaluating adjuvant systemic therapy: recommendations of Common-Sense Oncology and the European Organisation for Research and Treatment of Cancer
articles.abstract: The goal of adjuvant systemic therapy after locoregional treatment of cancer is to increase the probability of cure by eradicating micro-metastases. Adjuvant treatment adds side-effects and can impair health-related quality of life (HRQOL); this must be balanced against a reduction in the probability of recurrence, which has a substantial negative effect on HRQOL. Since many adjuvant therapies lead to small gains in relapse-free or overall survival, the severity and duration of treatment-related side-effects and their impact on patient functioning and overall HRQOL are relevant to clinical decision making.

articles.title: [Policy Review] Development of the Children's Oncology Group long-term follow-up guideline for cancer genetics evaluation in childhood cancer survivors
articles.abstract: Up to 12% of childhood cancer survivors have an underlying cancer predisposition syndrome (CPS). As a result, these childhood cancer survivors are at increased risk for developing and succumbing to subsequent malignant neoplasms. Identifying childhood cancer survivors with CPS is essential to improving overall outcomes by informing tailored approaches to cancer screening, treatment, and, for some, risk-reducing interventions. Despite these potential benefits, it is often unclear which childhood cancer survivors warrant referral for genetic counselling and germline genetic testing.

articles.title: [Policy Review] Curative-intent management of de novo metastatic nasopharyngeal carcinoma: an evidence-based consensus guideline from the International Collaborating Oncology Organisations
articles.abstract: Patients with de novo metastatic nasopharyngeal carcinoma were historically deemed incurable and treated with palliative intent. Emergence of potent systemic therapy in combination with local treatment for both locoregional and metastatic diseases has enabled long-term survival in some patients. This international guideline was developed through consensus-building by 54 experts from 46 centres across 18 countries or regions and endorsed by 17 oncology organisations. 32 recommendations across seven clinical domains were formulated, including 29 strong (≥80% agreement [consensus] or high quality of evidence) and three conditional recommendations (67–79% agreement).

articles.title: Human-centric preclinical models for CAR T cell therapy in solid tumors: Where patient-derived organoids fit
articles.abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell therapy has shown promising activity in solid tumors, yet translational progress remains limited by preclinical models that incompletely capture human tumor biology. Patient-derived organoids (PDOs) preserve key features of human tumors, including cellular heterogeneity and tissue architecture, thereby enabling functional evaluation of CAR T cell targets, next-generation approaches, resistance mechanisms, and selected safety considerations. We discuss how PDOs complement existing preclinical platforms to support CAR T cell development for solid tumors.

articles.title: Toward the next generation of CAR T cell therapies for cancer
articles.abstract: CAR T cell therapy has transformed the treatment of blood cancers but faces persistent challenges in solid tumors. In this review, Usta and Mackall synthesize clinical lessons, next-generation engineering strategies, and emerging in vivo manufacturing approaches to define opportunities for broader, safer, and more effective CAR T cell therapies.

articles.title: Anti-B7-H3 ADCs Take Center Stage against SCLC at WCLC.
articles.abstract: Separate phase III trials of the anti-B7-H3 antibody-drug conjugates tambotatug pelitecan and risvutatug rezetecan significantly improved overall survival, progression-free survival, and objective response rates compared with topotecan in patients with relapsed small-cell lung cancer. In a third trial, the combination of the investigational PD-L1 x VEGF-A bispecific antibody pumitamig plus the anti-B7-H3 ADC elfetabart drozuntecan showed encouraging early efficacy in SCLC across lines of therapy and doses. The studies were presented at the 2026 World Congress on Lung Cancer in Seoul, Republic of Korea.

articles.title: A Phase I First-Time-in-Human, Open-label Study of Nelistotug Administered to Patients with Advanced Solid Tumors.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: This first-in-human, nonrandomized, multicenter study investigated nelistotug [anti-cluster of differentiation (CD) 96 monoclonal antibody (mAb)] as monotherapy (arm A), in combination with dostarlimab [anti-programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1) mAb; arm B], and dostarlimab plus belrestotug [anti-T-cell immunoreceptor with Ig and immunoreceptor tyrosine-based inhibitory motif domains (TIGIT) mAb; arm F] in patients with recurrent or advanced solid tumors. PATIENTS AND METHODS: Patients received intravenous doses every 3 weeks of nelistotug 2.1 to 1,400 mg, nelistotug 70 to 1,400 mg plus dostarlimab 500 mg, or nelistotug 1,400 mg plus dostarlimab 500 mg plus belrestotug 400 mg in arms A, B, and F, respectively. Primary endpoints were dose-limiting toxicities (DLT) and adverse events (AE). Secondary endpoints included objective response rate, pharmacokinetics, and immunogenicity. Disease control rate and CD96 receptor occupancy were exploratory. RESULTS: Thirty-six, 33, and 3 patients were included in arms A, B, and F, respectively. No DLTs were observed in any arm, allowing for dose escalation to nelistotug maximum planned dose in arms A and B, with a recommended phase II dose of 1,400 mg. No treatment-related fatal AEs were observed. In arm B, 1 (3%) patient achieved a complete response and 1 (3%) achieved a partial response; no responses were observed in arms A and F. Nelistotug serum concentrations across doses were calculated to be sufficient to saturate the target in the tumor since >95% CD96 receptor occupancy was observed in peripheral blood immune cells. CONCLUSIONS: Nelistotug as monotherapy and in combination with dostarlimab and belrestotug had an acceptable safety and tolerability profile; however, efficacy was limited in this heavily pretreated patient population with advanced solid tumors.

articles.title: Colonoscopy surveillance after colorectal cancer surgery: meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Colonoscopy surveillance is recommended following colorectal cancer (CRC) surgery, yet the evidence supporting the recommendations has major quality issues. This study assessed the independent impact of colonoscopy surveillance within 5 years after CRC surgery. METHODS: A systematic review and meta-analysis were conducted. Medline, Scopus, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials were searched from inception until 18 June 2026 for randomized clinical trials comparing follow-up protocols including colonoscopy surveillance (intervention) to those without colonoscopy surveillance (control) within 5 years after CRC surgery. Risk of bias was assessed using the RoB 2 tool. Random-effects meta-analyses were conducted to estimate the strength of associations with recurrence detection, reoperation rate, and survival. The number needed to scope (NNS) to detect one recurrence and health economic considerations were estimated. The study protocol has been registered in PROSPERO. RESULTS: Of 4381 records, five trials with 2337 patients were included. Four trials enrolled patients between 1983 and 1994, predating subsequent advances in CRC treatment. All trials used additional surveillance modalities, leading to a high risk of bias. Follow-up protocols with colonoscopy were not associated with recurrence profile, with risk ratios (RRs) of 0.74 (95% confidence interval (c.i.) 0.32 to 1.69), 1.23 (95% c.i. 0.93 to 1.63), and 0.93 (95% c.i. 0.76 to 1.14) for intraluminal, locoregional, and distant recurrence, respectively. Colonoscopy during follow-up was associated with a higher rate of asymptomatic recurrence (RR 2.38; 95% c.i. 1.53 to 3.69). More curative-intent reoperations were performed in the intervention than control group (RR 1.66; 95% c.i. 1.16 to 2.37), but this was not translated into improved survival (hazard ratio 0.92; 95% c.i. 0.77 to 1.11). The NNS was 159 (95% c.i. 101 to 267), resulting in estimated cost per colonoscopy-detected recurrence of €104 100 (95% c.i. €66 200 to 174 900). CONCLUSION: Current evidence from randomized trials does not clearly demonstrate that postoperative colonoscopy surveillance improves survival, although interpretation is limited by the age of the trials and confounding from concurrent surveillance modalities. Contemporary randomized trials are required to better define the independent contribution of colonoscopy within modern multimodal surveillance pathways.

articles.title: Neoadjuvant Chemoimmunotherapy Improves Response Rates in Head and Neck Cancer.
articles.abstract: Despite the recent approval of perioperative pembrolizumab for locally advanced, resectable head and neck squamous cell carcinoma, response rates to immunotherapy are low. A recent single-arm phase II trial of neoadjuvant nivolumab in combination with carboplatin and paclitaxel demonstrated improved pathologic response rates compared with either chemotherapy or immunotherapy alone. See related article by Zinner et al., p. 4791.

articles.abstract: A 92-year-old man with a history of diffuse large B-cell lymphoma treated with chemoradiotherapy, and later with radiotherapy for an isolated cutaneous relapse with complete response, presented with a 1-month history of multiple asymptomatic erythematous-to-violaceous papules and nodules on the face, trunk, and upper limbs. Given his oncological history and previous skin involvement, lymphoma relapse was the leading diagnostic concern, with cutaneous metastases and sarcoidosis also considered. However, skin biopsies showed a non-Langerhans cell histiocytic infiltrate expressing CD45, CD68, and CD163, without CD1a, CD20, PAX5, S100, or Langerin expression.

articles.abstract: A patient with a history of lung adenocarcinoma had violaceous-to-brown cutaneous patches and plaques. Computed tomography showed splenomegaly and multicentric lymphadenopathy, and laboratory testing showed an elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate and levels of IgG, IgG4, IgA, and interleukin 6. What is the diagnosis and what would you do next?

articles.title: [Articles] Assessment of comprehensiveness of national cancer control plans using a multiagent artificial intelligence model: a global analysis
articles.abstract: Our analysis suggests that NCCP comprehensiveness varies substantially between countries with consistent weaknesses in financing, outcome measurement, and contextual analysis. A shared health systems framework and scalable AI appraisal tools, such as PRISM, could support more complete, comparable, and actionable plans to strengthen cancer control globally by providing the possibility for rapid analysis of comprehensiveness of NCCPs and generation of timely, achievable, and evidence-informed, context-specific plans that use the latest data.

articles.title: [Articles] Global uptake of essential cancer medicines with and without complex genomic diagnostics: a retrospective observational study
articles.abstract: These findings should be interpreted as evidence of associations not causality, suggesting differences in quantity uptake of essential cancer medicines along two structural dimensions: fewer countries showed uptake of essential cancer medicines in lower-GDP countries than in middle-GDP and high-GDP countries and medicines requiring complex genomic diagnostics had lower uptake, with the lowest uptake in lower-GDP countries. The results suggest that, as precision oncology medicines become increasingly represented in the WHO EML, EML inclusion alone could be insufficient to enable patient access.

articles.title: [Articles] Global health expenditures on cancer control: a cross-sectional analysis
articles.abstract: Our findings indicate high variability of per-capita health expenditure on cancer control globally and generally low expenditure levels, particularly in lower-middle-income and low-income countries and territories. The paucity of publicly available expenditure data on cancer control indicates the need for production of detailed NHAs that include disease-specific expenditures to ensure availability of regular, comparable, and reliable data.

articles.title: Chronotherapy with immune checkpoint inhibitors: The knowns, the unknowns, and the contested
articles.abstract: Emerging data indicate that immune checkpoint inhibitors can exhibit time-of-day-dependent effects in pre-clinical models. Furthermore, multiple retrospective clinical trials associate earlier anti-tumor treatment timing with improved outcomes. However, key questions remain regarding the reproducibility of these findings, the underlying mechanisms, and their clinical implications. This commentary discusses these open questions and provides an outlook on the field.

articles.title: γδ T cells BiTE back at small cell lung cancer
articles.abstract: In this issue of Cancer Cell, Ng et al. characterize and leverage cytotoxic γδ T cells in small cell lung cancer to overcome unsuccessful checkpoint blockade immunotherapy. Engaging Vδ2+ cells with a bispecific T cell engager (BiTE) bypasses the challenge of low MHC-I expression and ineffective CD8+ T cells.

articles.title: Microbial cues for a stem-like lymphoid niche
articles.abstract: While tertiary lymphoid structures (TLSs) broadly correlate with immunotherapy efficacy, their functional heterogeneity can translate into divergent clinical outcomes. In this issue of Cancer Cell, Hu et al. uncover a microbiota-orchestrated stem-like lymphoid niche in which CD70+ ILC2s sustain progenitor exhausted T cells, and their findings redefine the functional organization underlying TLS-associated antitumor immunity.

articles.title: Teamwork makes the dream work? Ensemble learning in computational pathology
articles.abstract: In this issue of Cancer Cell, Luo et al. report an ensemble approach that integrates five pretrained pathology foundation models into a slide-level representation to exploit their complementary information, yielding improvements in tumor subtyping, biomarker, and therapy-response prediction. This shows the potential of ensemble and multimodal approaches in computational pathology.

articles.title: Hitting KRAS G12D without the gut punch: Can immunotherapy make it last?
articles.abstract: In this issue of Cancer Cell, Shi et al. report encouraging early-phase results combining HRS-4642, an allele-specific KRAS G12D inhibitor, with the PD-L1 inhibitor adebrelimab in previously treated metastatic pancreatic cancer. The intravenous combination was safe and well tolerated, notably sparing patients the gastrointestinal toxicity common to oral KRAS inhibitors, and achieved a promising 43% response rate at the recommended dose.

articles.title: Beyond genes and hotspots: Protein-informed interpretation of cancer mutations
articles.abstract: Interpreting the biological and clinical significance of somatic mutations in cancer genomes remains challenging. In this issue of Cancer Cell, Hyeon et al. identify and map significantly mutated regions to protein domains and structural features, establishing a proteo-genomics framework for interpreting cancer mutations beyond genes and hotspots.

articles.title: The wu wei of brain metastases: When the gift of a pause is also a vulnerability
articles.abstract: In this issue of Cancer Cell, García-Gómez et al. show that brain-seeding cancer cells exploit an MXD4-dependent proliferative pause that enables survival under stress before metastatic outgrowth. By restraining MYC and activating protective stress responses, this pause becomes an Achilles’ heel, potentially targetable to eradicate micrometastases before clinical relapse.

articles.title: Tumor cells recruit macrophage bodyguards to outlast chemotherapy
articles.abstract: In Cell Press Blue, Carvalho et al. identify spatially organized tumor-macrophage niches, EMT-like CD44high cancer cells paired with SPP1/PARP14high macrophages, that drive chemoresistance in bladder cancer. PARP14 inhibition can flip this protective niche into an inflammatory, cisplatin-sensitizing state.

articles.title: Beyond BMI: The diet-microbiome context of the obesity paradox
articles.abstract: In Nature, Desharnais et al. show that in diverse mouse models, anti-PD-1 sensitivity is more closely linked to diet-microbiome-metabolite ecosystem than to obesity-associated metabolic dysfunction. Their findings reinforce body mass index (BMI) as an incomplete proxy for host biology and suggest strategies to improve anti-PD-1 efficacy without inducing obesity.

articles.title: γδ T cells modulate anti-tumor immunity in small cell lung cancer
articles.abstract: Ng et al. show that γδ T cells infiltrate SCLC and have cancer-fighting abilities. These cells can be harnessed through multiple therapeutics to kill SCLC, including through MHC-independent recognition mechanisms via BTN2A1. Notably, γδ T cell infiltration is clinically relevant in SCLC, with high levels predictive of improved outcomes with αPD-L1.

articles.title: Ensemble learning of pathology foundation models for precision oncology
articles.abstract: Luo et al. develop ELF, a framework that ensembles five pathology foundation models to generate unified representations from whole-slide images. Trained on nearly 54,000 slides across 20 anatomical sites, ELF outperforms individual foundation models in disease classification, biomarker detection, and prediction of response to chemotherapy, targeted therapy, and immunotherapy.

articles.title: UniCure: A multi-modal model for predicting personalized cancer therapy response
articles.abstract: Chen et al. present UniCure, a multi-modal foundation model that predicts drug-induced transcriptomic responses across diverse cellular contexts. By bridging cancer cell line data with patient-derived models, UniCure enables personalized drug prioritization and patient stratification, with its predicted therapeutic rankings correlating strongly with clinical survival outcomes in real-world cohorts.

articles.title: Myeloid reprogramming generates myeloid-derived activating cells to potentiate radiotherapy and suppress metastasis
articles.abstract: Ji et al. show that radiotherapy induces a TET2-dependent epitranscriptomic program in myeloid cells that promotes immunosuppressive M-MDSC differentiation. TET2 loss preserves caRNA m5C-MBD6 signaling, restores IRF3-IFN-I activation, generates myeloid-derived activating cells, and enhances radiotherapy-induced antitumor immunity.

articles.title: Intratumoral Bacillus cereus orchestrates stem-like lymphoid niches to potentiate immunotherapy response in hepatocellular carcinoma
articles.abstract: Hu et al. integrate spatial multi-omics to identify stem-like lymphoid niches (SLNs) organized by CD70+ ILC2s and Tpex cells that predict PD-1/PD-L1 immunotherapy responses in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). They reveal that Bacillus cereus-PI-PLC increases SLN abundance and synergizes with PD-L1 blockade, highlighting microbiota-driven enhancement of cancer immunotherapy through SLNs therapeutically in HCC.

articles.title: Proteo-genomics-guided interpretation of somatic mutations in cancer genomes
articles.abstract: Hyeon et al. integrate protein structures with population-scale cancer genomics data to characterize significantly mutated regions in 173 cancer-relevant genes. These regions align with functional domains, three-dimensional structural constraints, and gene-specific biology, providing a framework for classifying mutation patterns in cancer genes and prioritizing sparsely annotated variants for clinical interpretation.

articles.title: A transient MXD4-dependent proliferative pause enables survival of brain micrometastases
articles.abstract: García-Gómez et al. identify a transient state, termed the proliferative pause, that enables the survival of micrometastases during vascular co-option by buffering organ-imposed stress. Targeting vulnerabilities associated with this state suppresses metastatic progression and relapse, revealing opportunities for preventive intervention.

articles.title: Chemotherapy enhances cancer vaccine efficacy and expands stem-like TCF1+CD8+ T cells
articles.abstract: Noblecourt et al. show that chemotherapy acts as an immunological adjuvant by expanding TCF1+CD8+ T cells during vaccine priming, thereby enhancing vaccine-induced anti-tumor immunity. These findings provide a rationale for combining chemotherapy, cancer vaccines, and PD-1 blockade in the clinic.

articles.title: Neoadjuvant Apalutamide With or Without Abiraterone Acetate Plus Prednisone and Gonadotropin-Releasing Hormone Agonist Prior to Nerve-Sparing Radical Prostatectomy in High-Risk Prostate Cancer: Protocol for a Randomized Phase 2 Trial.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Radical prostatectomy (RP) is an accepted, definitive treatment for appropriately selected men with high-risk localized prostate cancer (PCa). However, neoadjuvant androgen receptor inhibition prior to RP is not currently the standard of care. Wide resection of the neurovascular bundles may improve local oncologic control but can adversely affect postoperative erectile function and urinary continence. Apalutamide directly inhibits the androgen receptor, while abiraterone acetate inhibits cytochrome P450 17A1-mediated androgen synthesis and is often administered with prednisone. Gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) agonists further suppress testicular androgen production. Intensified androgen pathway inhibition prior to surgery may therefore downstage localized disease and facilitate bilateral nerve-sparing RP. OBJECTIVE: This study was defined to evaluate whether 3 months of neoadjuvant apalutamide-based therapy before RP improves postoperative potency recovery by 12 months compared with immediate RP in men with high-risk localized PCa. Secondary objectives include evaluation of postoperative continence, pathological outcomes, biochemical recurrence, perioperative outcomes, and quality of life (QoL). METHODS: This is a prospective, multicenter, randomized phase 2 clinical trial (ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT02949284). Eligible patients with high-risk PCa were randomized 1:1:1 to (1) apalutamide 240 mg daily for 3 months followed by RP, (2) apalutamide 240 mg daily with abiraterone acetate 1000 mg plus prednisone 10 mg daily and a GnRH agonist for 3 months followed by RP, or (3) immediate RP without neoadjuvant therapy. The primary end point is potency recovery by 12 months postoperatively, defined as the ability to penetrate in sexual intercourse in more than half of attempts. Secondary end points include continence recovery, pathological response, positive surgical margins, biochemical recurrence, perioperative outcomes, and QoL. The primary comparisons evaluate each experimental arm against the surgery-only arm. Pairwise comparisons of the primary end point will use 1-sided Fisher exact tests with a Bonferroni adjustment. Additional continuous and categorical outcomes will be analyzed using appropriate nonparametric or categorical tests, and biochemical recurrence-free survival will be assessed using Kaplan-Meier analysis. RESULTS: As of March 2026, patient enrollment has been completed. A total of 96 patients provided consent and were screened, 88 were randomized, and 73 received the assigned treatment and were included in the final analysis cohort. Study accrual began on June 20, 2017, and enrollment was completed in June 2024. The prespecified postoperative follow-up period extended beyond 24 months, with a study data cutoff date of June 30, 2025. Data collection for the primary and secondary outcomes has been completed, with final expected results anticipated in January 2027. CONCLUSIONS: This randomized phase 2 trial was designed to assess whether short-term androgen pathway inhibition can improve postoperative functional outcomes while maintaining oncologic outcomes in men undergoing nerve-sparing RP for high-risk localized PCa.

articles.title: Longitudinal remodeling of the tumor-immune microenvironment during regorafenib, nivolumab, and chemotherapy in advanced gastric cancer.
