articles.title: A phase 2 study of tipifarnib in children and young adults with tumors harboring HRAS genomic alterations: NCI-COG Pediatric MATCH trial (APEC1621M).
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: APEC1621 arm M, a subprotocol of the NCI-COG Pediatric MATCH clinical trial, is a phase 2 study evaluating tipifarnib, a farnesyl transferase inhibitor, in patients with relapsed or refractory solid tumors harboring HRAS mutations at codons G12, G13, Q61, or A146 (NCT04284774). METHODS: Patients identified by the MATCH screening protocol and enrolled to the arm M subprotocol received tipifarnib at 350 mg/m2/dose (maximum 600 mg/dose) orally twice daily on an intermittent dosing schedule (days 1-7 and 15-21, every 28 days) until disease progression or intolerable toxicity. The primary aim was to determine the objective response rate (ORR), and secondary objectives included estimating progression-free survival (PFS) and assessing the tolerability of tipifarnib on the intermittent dosing schedule in children. RESULTS: Seven patients matched to the tipifarnib subprotocol and five patients (71%) enrolled. Two matched patients were ineligible for treatment. Diagnoses for the enrolled patients were rhabdomyosarcoma (n = 4) and angiosarcoma (n = 1). HRAS mutations identified in those tumors included G13R (n = 2) and G12S, G12C, and Q61L (n = 1 each). Treatment was associated with grade 1/2 adverse events (AE) consistent with those expected from prior studies. Grade 3 or higher AEs on treatment were disease progression, dyspnea, and pleural effusion, not related to protocol therapy. One patient had stable disease (SD) at the end of cycle 2 and remained on protocol therapy for 4 cycles. There were no objective responses (OR). CONCLUSIONS: This US cooperative group study was successful at identifying pediatric patients with tumors that harbored oncogenic mutations in HRAS. The frequency of the mutations identified and patients enrolled was lower than anticipated, and the study closed before accrual was complete. The adverse effect profile of tipifarnib in pediatric patients on the intermittent dosing schedule was acceptable. Limited single-agent efficacy of tipifarnib was observed in this biomarker-selected cohort of refractory pediatric tumors.

articles.title: [Comment] Multiple standards of care in non-small-cell lung cancer after EGFR-TKI therapy: progress, fragmentation, or inevitability?
articles.abstract: The treatment landscape of EGFR-mutated non-small-cell lung cancer harbouring exon 19 deletion or L858R mutations has advanced remarkably over the past two decades. Although acquired resistance to EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) is inevitable in most patients, novel compounds such as bispecific antibodies and antibody–drug conjugates (ADCs) have expanded the armamentarium of options after EGFR-TKI therapy. Following the global MARIPOSA-2 trial that showed superior progression-free survival (PFS) of amivantamab plus platinum–pemetrexed chemotherapy over platinum–pemetrexed chemotherapy alone in patients who have progressed on osimertinib,1 this is the second-line option preferred by major guidelines including the National Comprehensive Cancer Network and the European Society for Medical Oncology.

articles.title: [Editorial] Sweating the details in exercise oncology
articles.abstract: The benefit of exercise alongside cancer treatment and recovery has primarily rested on association. However, two randomised trials, CHALLENGE and STAMINA, now supply the causal evidence that exercise oncology lacked. The pressing question is now one of implementation. STAMINA has already led to free exercise programmes for men undergoing treatment for prostate cancer in the UK and the European Society for Medical Oncology has updated their guidelines as a result of the CHALLENGE study.

articles.title: [Comment] Iberdomide for minimal residual disease-negative myeloma—from underdog to the spotlight
articles.abstract: The introduction of thalidomide and its derivatives—lenalidomide, followed by pomalidomide—has improved the therapeutic arsenal for multiple myeloma for more than two decades. These immunomodulators bind to cereblon, a component of the CRL4-cereblon E3 ubiquitin ligase complex, which results in the targeted degradation of the transcription factors Ikaros and Aiolos.1,2 Iberdomide belongs to the next generation of drugs, known as cereblon E3 ligase modulators. Its chemical structure is extended by an additional benzyl moiety bearing a morpholine group—which increases the molecular volume and the contact surface with cereblon, thereby enhancing its affinity and degradation potency compared with conventional immunomodulators.

articles.title: [Comment] Time to say goodbye to full-field digital mammography in population-based screening?
articles.abstract: 51 (96%) of 53 countries in the WHO European Region have national breast cancer screening programmes. Globally, 63% of all nations have established breast cancer screening programmes.1 Most of the European screening programmes are organised nationally and are population-based, focusing on women older than 50 years.1 Full-field digital mammography is the gold standard screening modality used in these programmes because of its clinical efficiency and cost-effectiveness.2

articles.title: [Comment] Comprehensiveness of national cancer control plans
articles.abstract: Cancer poses a disproportionate disease burden across different country populations. Beyond large international differences in cancer incidence, cancer survival varies globally, even between countries within the same continent or among those with publicly funded health-care systems.1–3 Therefore, much research in recent years has rightly focused on how countries with a relatively poor record in cancer control could narrow the gap separating them from high-performing peers.

articles.title: [Comment] The unfulfilled promise of effective cancer medicines priced beyond reach
articles.abstract: Every year, pivotal clinical trials are reported, showing major advances in cancer treatment. At the American Society of Clinical Oncology (ASCO) 2026 conference, results from the RASolute302 trial for patients with advanced pancreatic cancer established daraxonrasib, a RAS(ON) inhibitor, as a watershed moment in oncology.1 Among previously treated patients, daraxonrasib improved median overall survival by 7 months compared with chemotherapy and improved quality of life. Given that pancreatic cancer is among the most lethal of all cancers, the target was hitherto considered undruggable, and that the disease is accompanied by considerable suffering, this treatment was appropriately celebrated as a landmark success of drug development.

articles.title: [Comment] Rare earth elements and the fragile promise of cancer theranostics
articles.abstract: Radionuclide theranostics is transforming oncology by enabling more personalised treatment based on tumour biology. The approach pairs tumour-specific vectors with diagnostic and therapeutic radionuclides. Theranostics enables clinicians to confirm tumour targeting via molecular imaging before delivering targeted radiation with the same vector. Over the past decade, this approach has transformed treatment for neuroendocrine tumours and prostate cancer and is now expanding into additional malignancies and earlier stages of disease.

articles.abstract: Malawi's National Cancer Centre, opened in July, 2025, with support from the International Atomic Energy Agency's (IAEA) Rays of Hope initiative, is intended to bring several cancer services together in one facility. articles.title: [News] India reaches 8 million milestone in HPV campaign
articles.abstract: Earlier this month, India surpassed 8 million doses of the human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine, Gardasil-4, administered under a nationwide campaign launched earlier this year. The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare described the milestone as an important step forward in their goal of reducing cervical cancer in a country that accounts for roughly a quarter of global deaths from the disease. Four states have already reached 100% coverage of their target populations. However, the national picture is uneven, and experts say sustaining momentum will require overcoming vaccine hesitancy, misinformation, and the logistical demands of reaching eligible girls across a vast and diverse country.

articles.title: TIM3 Blockade with Hypomethylating Therapy Restores NK Cell and Cytotoxic CD4+ T-cell Activity in Patients with AML or MDS.
articles.abstract: Occasional complete responses (CR) to immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy demonstrate that acute myeloid leukemia (AML) and myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS) can be immunosensitive when appropriately targeted. In this study, we analyzed patients with AML/MDS (n = 14) who were treated with the anti-TIM3 sabatolimab and the hypomethylating agent decitabine in a phase Ib clinical trial (NCT03066648) using single-cell RNA and T-cell receptor (TCR) sequencing (n = 6) and functional coculture assays. Unlike T cell-restricted CTLA4 and PD1, TIM3 was broadly expressed across natural killer (NK) cell, myeloid cell, and T-cell populations. Therapy induced the expansion of cytotoxic NK cell subsets and enhanced type I IFN signaling. Fewer than 1% of bone marrow CD8+ T cells displayed a canonical exhaustion phenotype, and treatment preferably expanded small CD8+ T-cell clones in responders. Responders exhibited greater expansion of cytotoxic CD4+ T cells and B cells, as exemplified by a patient with preexisting CD4+ T-cell large granular lymphocyte leukemia (T-LGLL) achieving an outstanding CR lasting 23 months. More than 20% of this patient's lymphocytes were T-LGLL cells expressing a TCR capable of recognizing autologous blasts. Overall, our results suggest that anti-TIM3 combined with decitabine engages a distinct mechanism of immune activation compared with anti-PD-1 and anti-CTLA4, preferentially expanding NK cell and CD4+ T-cell populations.

articles.title: Neoadjuvant PD-L1/TGF-β blockade can rapidly disrupt the tumor stroma in head and neck cancer patients.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUNDTGF-β drives fibroblast activation in cancer and is a resistance biomarker to PD-1/PD-L1 blockade.METHODSFocusing on the tumor stroma, we characterized the impact of neoadjuvant treatment with bintrafusp alfa (BA), a dual PD-L1 and TGF-β inhibitor, in a window-of-opportunity study with 6 patients with head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC). Tumor biopsies before treatment and 3 weeks after therapy were analyzed using scRNA-seq, imaging, and spatial transcriptomics.RESULTSAfter treatment, we observed significantly decreased levels of activated LRRC15+ cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs), remodeled stromal architecture with reduced collagen I and XII content, and increased CD8+ T cell infiltration in immune-excluded tumors. These changes were independently confirmed in an additional neoadjuvant BA-treated cohort of 6 patients with HNSCC. The drastic CAF and stromal compartment reduction observed indicated a fibroblast depletion rather than a fibroblast polarization shift.CONCLUSIONWhile our final clinical cohort does not allow assessment of the treatment effect, this study demonstrated that targeting TGF-β in patients can disrupt the tumor stroma within a short time frame. Further trials and novel biomarkers are now needed to select patients who could benefit.TRIAL REGISTRATIONClinicalTrials.gov NCT04428047.FUNDINGMerck KGaA, ARC Emerging Leaders in Oncology, ANR-10-IDEX-0001-02 PSL, Centre d'Investigation Clinique IGR-Curie 1428, Site de Recherche Intégrée sur le Cancer (INCa-DGOS-Inserm-ITMO cancer_18000), French Government "Investissements d'Avenir" program, France 2030 program, Fondation pour la Recherche Médicale, Marie Skłodowska-Curie grant agreement 847718, Cooperative Research and Development Agreement with EMD Serono, and NIH (ZIA BC 010666).

articles.title: Immunologic Timing and Therapeutic Sequencing of Locoregional Therapy and Immunotherapy in Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
articles.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitor combinations have improved outcomes in hepatocellular carcinoma, but durable benefit remains uneven and the optimal integration of locoregional therapy is unresolved. Local interventions can release tumor antigens, alter vascular and stromal barriers, and recruit innate and adaptive immune cells. These effects can coexist with tissue repair, angiogenic signaling, myeloid recruitment, and renewed checkpoint expression. This narrative review examines therapeutic timing for clinicians and translational researchers. A targeted PubMed search, publisher reports, and reference checking informed the revision; studies were selected for relevance to human immune kinetics, clinical schedules, safety, and biomarker validation. This review compares thermal ablation, transarterial chemoembolization, yttrium-90 radioembolization, irreversible electroporation, and stereotactic body radiotherapy; evaluates checkpoint inhibition before, after, or overlapping local treatment; and assesses candidate scheduling biomarkers. Human studies document selected immune changes, while phase 3 trials show that some treatment combinations extend progression-free survival. However, these trials do not isolate timing, and observational schedule comparisons cannot establish a causal advantage or a universal interval. A modality- and patient-specific hypothesis is therefore discussed in which measured immune state and hepatic reserve could inform future scheduling trials. No biomarker-triggered schedule has demonstrated clinical utility. Serial tissue and blood sampling, pharmacokinetic assessment, and schedule-specific randomization are needed before an immunogenic window can guide routine care.

articles.title: Prognostic value of the systemic inflammation response index (SIRI) in glioma: A meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To systematically evaluate the predictive value of systemic inflammation response index (SIRI) for the prognosis of glioma patients. METHODS: PubMed, Cochrane Library, EMBASE, and Web of Science databases were searched to collect literature on the relationship between SIRI and glioma prognosis from database inception to July 2026. The primary outcome measures were overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival (PFS). STATA 15.0 and Review Manager 5.4 software were used, and random-effects models were employed with pooled hazard ratios (HR) and their 95% confidence intervals (CI) to assess the prognostic value of SIRI. Subgroup analyses, sensitivity analyses, and publication bias assessments were performed. RESULTS: Eight retrospective cohort studies involving 1778 glioma patients were included, forming 12 comparison groups for OS analysis and 4 comparison groups for PFS analysis. Meta-analysis results showed that a higher SIRI was significantly associated with poorer OS (pooled HR = 1.79, 95% CI: 1.34-2.38, P < 0.0001) and PFS (pooled HR = 1.46, 95% CI: 1.18-1.81, P = 0.0005) in glioma patients. Subgroup analysis showed that the prognostic value of SIRI for OS was not significant in the European population subgroup, suggesting that the association may be modulated by geographic region. Sensitivity analysis confirmed the robustness of the results. Egger's test indicated publication bias in the OS analysis (P = 0.0001), but no significant bias was found in the PFS analysis. CONCLUSION: This meta-analysis suggests that elevated SIRI is associated with poorer OS and PFS in glioma patients, although this association was not consistently observed across all subgroups, particularly in European populations. These findings highlight the need for further validation with standardized cut-off values in diverse populations.

articles.title: Can Esophagectomy be Safely Avoided After Clinical Complete Response in Esophageal Squamous Cell Carcinoma? Response Assessment, Active Surveillance, and Salvage in the Immunotherapy Era.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Clinical complete response (cCR) after chemoradiotherapy or immunotherapy-containing neoadjuvant treatment is increasingly encountered in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC). We examine whether esophagectomy can be safely deferred or avoided in selected complete responders, distinguishing prediction of pathologic complete response (pCR) from the higher confidence required to omit surgery. RECENT FINDINGS: The phase III SANO trial showed non-inferior 2-year overall survival with active surveillance versus standard surgery after cCR following neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy, with early quality-of-life benefits; however, approximately three quarters of participants had adenocarcinoma. The ESCC-specific preSINO study showed that bite-on-bite biopsies, endoscopic ultrasonography with fine-needle aspiration, and PET/CT reduce but do not eliminate missed residual disease. In a biomarker analysis nested within preSINO, adding tumor-informed circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) to conventional evaluation increased sensitivity for non-pCR to approximately 92-93%; this is not independent validation. Neoadjuvant immunotherapy, including ESCORT-NEO and PALACE regimens, has increased pCR rates, but response-assessment accuracy has not been validated in these treatment contexts. Earlier ESCC trials of definitive chemoradiotherapy with selective salvage established organ preservation conceptually; the modern question is whether surveillance can be individualized after rigorously defined cCR. Active surveillance after cCR is now a credible option within structured programs, but routine omission of esophagectomy in ESCC is not yet standard care. Organ preservation should be viewed as a longitudinal residual-disease exclusion program with predefined rescue triggers rather than a one-time declaration of cCR. ESCC-specific, treatment-context-specific trials integrating standardized endoscopic and nodal assessment, PET/CT, serial ctDNA, and salvage outcomes are needed before immunotherapy-associated cCR can routinely justify nonoperative management.

articles.title: Prognostic Value of the Preoperative Systemic Immune-Inflammation Index for Overall Survival After Surgical Resection for Gallbladder Cancer: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: The systemic immune-inflammation index (SII) reflects the balance between tumor-promoting inflammation and antitumor immunity, but its prognostic role in gallbladder cancer (GBC) remains uncertain. We aimed to evaluate the prognostic value of preoperative SII in patients undergoing resection for GBC. METHODS: This systematic review and meta-analysis was reported in accordance with PRISMA 2020. PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and Scopus were searched from inception through November 1, 2025. For the primary meta-analysis, the most comprehensively adjusted hazard ratio (HR) was selected when available; a directly reported univariable HR was used when no adjusted SII-specific estimate was reported. Sensitivity and supplementary analyses pooled multivariable-adjusted and univariable HRs separately. Log-transformed HRs were pooled using random-effects models with restricted maximum likelihood estimation. RESULTS: Seven retrospective cohorts comprising 2,153 patients were included in the systematic review, of which six studies comprising 2,067 patients contributed directly comparable high-versus-low HRs to the primary meta-analysis. Higher preoperative SII was associated with poorer overall survival (OS) (pooled HR 2.06; 95% CI 1.70-2.51; I² = 3.6%). The association remained significant in the sensitivity analysis restricted to five studies reporting multivariable-adjusted HRs (pooled adjusted HR 2.10; 95% CI 1.39-3.20; I² = 22.0%). The supplementary univariable analysis also demonstrated an association with poorer OS (pooled HR 3.11; 95% CI 1.68-5.75; I² = 75.2%). One study reporting only a continuous per-unit HR was synthesized narratively. CONCLUSIONS: Higher preoperative SII is associated with poorer OS after resection for GBC. Its incremental value for clinical risk stratification requires prospective evaluation and independent external validation. SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: PROSPERO CRD420251185808.

articles.title: Oncologic efficacy and safety of stereotactic body radiotherapy for oligometastatic non-small cell lung cancer: a systemic meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: With the increasing clinical interest on local consolidative therapies for oligometastasis (OM), stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT) has emerged as a definitive and optimal treatment modality. This study stratifies oligoprogressive (OPD), oligorecurrent (ORD), and oligopersistent (OPSD) states-alongside single-lesion subgroup analyses-to systematically evaluate the efficacy and safety of SBRT for oligometastatic NSCLC. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This meta-analysis was conducted utilizing the Pubmed, Embase and Medline. The quantitative synthesis included 18 eligible studies comprising a total of 1,105 patients. The clinical endpoints assessed were overall survival (OS), progression-free survival (PFS), local control (LC), and the incidence of severe (grade 3 or higher) treatment-related toxicities. RESULTS: The pooled estimates demonstrated robust oncological outcomes; 2-year OS of 60.0% (95% CI, 50.4-68.8%), 1-year PFS of 65.8% (95% CI, 52.7-76.8%), and 2-year LC rate of 74.2% (95% CI, 63.9-82.4%). The incidence of severe toxicities (grade ≥ 3) was 4.5%, predominantly manifesting as radiation pneumonitis and esophagitis. Subgroup analyses revealed that a higher prevalence of single-metastatic lesions (> 59%) exhibited a borderline positive trend toward superior 2-year OS (67.5% vs. 47.8%, p = 0.069). CONCLUSION: This meta-analysis indicates that SBRT yields favorable treatment outcomes for patients with oligometastatic NSCLC with manageable toxicities. articles.title: Sex difference in survival benefits of immune checkpoint inhibitors in advanced non-small cell lung cancer: A meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Whether sex influences the survival benefit of immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) in advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) remains uncertain. METHODS: We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, and Scopus up to April 1, 2026, for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing ICIs with chemotherapy and reporting overall survival (OS) or progression-free survival (PFS) stratified by sex. A random-effects model was used for meta-analysis. RESULTS: Sixty-three publications (reporting 42 phase 3 RCTs) involving 25,827 patients (18,772 male; 7,055 female) were included. Compared with chemotherapy, ICIs significantly improved both OS and PFS in males (OS: HR 0.74 [95% CI 0.71-0.78]; PFS: HR 0.59 [95% CI 0.54-0.64]) and females (OS: HR 0.83 [95% CI 0.77-0.90]; PFS: HR 0.76 [95% CI 0.66-0.86]). Pooled treatment-by-sex interaction analyses demonstrated significantly greater OS (interaction HR = 0.90 [95% CI 0.84-0.97]; P = 0.01) and PFS (interaction HR = 0.82 [95% CI 0.73-0.92]; P = 0.0006) benefits in males than in females. In subgroup analyses, sex‑based differences in OS reached statistical significance in patients receiving ICI monotherapy (P = 0.02), including those treated with anti‑PD‑1 monotherapy (P = 0.04) and those with PD‑L1 expression ≥50% (P = 0.02). However, these differences did not persist after the False Discovery Rate (FDR) correction (adjusted P = 0.07, 0.10, and 0.07, respectively). In contrast, sex‑based differences in PFS remained statistically significant after FDR correction in the ICI monotherapy (adjusted P = 0.001), anti‑PD‑1 monotherapy (adjusted P = 0.001), and PD‑L1 ≥ 50% (adjusted P = 0.004) subgroups. No significant sex‑based differences in either OS or PFS were observed among patients treated with ICI plus chemotherapy. CONCLUSIONS: Although ICIs are superior to chemotherapy in both sexes, the PFS benefit of ICI monotherapy appears to be attenuated in females relative to males. Given the imbalances in baseline confounders coupled with the underrepresentation of females in the included trials, these findings should be interpreted with caution and warrant confirmation in future RCTs designed specifically to investigate sex‑based differences.

articles.title: Effects of nutrition counseling on quality of life in adults with cancer: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Cancer and its treatments can often reduce patients' quality of life (QoL). Nutrition counseling, as a potential adjunctive intervention, may promote dietary behavior change and alleviate treatment-related burdens. However, the existing evidence regarding its effectiveness in improving QoL among adults with cancer remains inconclusive. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the effects of nutrition counseling on QoL in adults with cancer. METHODS: We systematically searched PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, the Cochrane Library, Scopus, and the ClinicalTrials.gov registry from inception to August 23, 2026. Eligible studies were randomized controlled trials evaluating the effects of nutrition counseling on QoL in adults with cancer. Effect sizes were estimated as standardized mean differences (SMDs) using Hedges' g with small-sample correction and pooled using a DerSimonian-Laird random-effects model to obtain summary estimates with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Sensitivity analyses and subgroup analyses were also conducted to assess the robustness of the pooled estimates and explore potential sources of heterogeneity. RESULTS: A total of 20 trials involving 1,668 participants were included in the review, with 1,301 participants contributing post-intervention QoL data to the meta-analysis. The pooled effect of nutrition counseling on QoL was SMD = 0.71 (95% CI: 0.35-1.07; p < 0.001), with substantial heterogeneity (I² = 88.7%; τ² = 0.587). The 95% prediction interval ranged from - 0.94 to 2.36, indicating that the magnitude and consistency of effects may vary across settings. Subgroup analyses showed higher pooled effect estimates in studies conducted in Asia (SMD = 1.42; 95% CI: 0.70-2.15; p < 0.001), developing countries (SMD = 1.57; 95% CI: 0.75-2.38; p < 0.001), and Eastern cultural backgrounds (SMD = 1.42; 95% CI: 0.70-2.15; p < 0.001), and among studies with a mean baseline BMI < 25 kg/m CONCLUSIONS: Nutrition counseling may improve QoL among adults with cancer, but the very low certainty of evidence and substantial heterogeneity limit confidence in the magnitude and consistency of this effect. Future high-quality studies are warranted to confirm these findings and clarify how clinical and contextual factors influence the effectiveness of nutrition counseling. SYSTEMATIC REVIEW​ REGISTRATION: PROSPERO registration no. CRD420251165789. Cancer and its treatments can adversely affect patients’ quality of life (QoL). Nutrition counseling, as a supportive intervention, may support dietary management and potentially improve quality of life; however, its effectiveness in improving QoL among adults with cancer remains uncertain. This study aimed to evaluate the effects of nutrition counseling on QoL and explore whether its effects varied across different populations and clinical settings. To ensure a focused assessment of nutrition counseling, we excluded studies in which other nutritional approaches, such as nutritional supplementation or enteral/parenteral nutrition, were evaluated without a clearly defined counseling component. The synthesis of 20 randomized controlled trials suggested that nutrition counseling may improve QoL among adults with cancer. However, substantial variation was observed across studies, indicating uncertainty regarding the consistency and magnitude of the observed effects, and the certainty of evidence was rated as very low. Subgroup analyses suggested potential differences across populations and settings, although these findings were based on study-level comparisons, involved overlapping classifications, and should be considered exploratory. Further high-quality studies are warranted to confirm these findings, assess their clinical significance, and clarify the factors underlying variation in intervention effects.

articles.title: Comparative efficacy and safety of second- and later-line BRAF-targeted regimens in BRAF V600E-mutant metastatic colorectal cancer: A systematic review and network meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: BRAF V600E mutations occur in approximately 8 to 12% of metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC) cases and define an aggressive phenotype with poor prognosis. While the BEACON CRC trial established encorafenib-based combinations as effective second-line options, direct head-to-head comparisons among available BRAF-targeted regimens are lacking. This network meta-analysis (NMA) compared the relative efficacy and safety of second- and later-line BRAF-targeted regimens in BRAF V600E-mutant mCRC. METHODS: PubMed, Embase, Cochrane CENTRAL, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched from inception through January 2026. Eligible studies enrolled adult patients with BRAF V600E-mutant mCRC receiving second- or later-line BRAF-targeted therapy and reported time-to-event survival outcomes. A frequentist NMA was conducted under a random-effects model using the netmeta package in R. Hazard ratios (HRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled for progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS). Where HRs were unavailable, individual patient data were reconstructed from Kaplan-Meier curves using the Guyot method. Treatment ranking used P-scores, with irinotecan plus cetuximab as the reference comparator. RESULTS: Four trials enrolling 922 patients across 9 treatment arms were included. All 4 experimental regimens demonstrated significant PFS benefit over irinotecan plus cetuximab. Encorafenib plus cetuximab plus alpelisib ranked highest for PFS (HR 0.33, 95% CI 0.15-0.71; P-score 0.789), followed by encorafenib plus binimetinib plus cetuximab (EBC; HR 0.38, 95% CI 0.29-0.49), encorafenib plus cetuximab (EC; HR 0.40, 95% CI 0.31-0.50), and vemurafenib plus irinotecan plus cetuximab (HR 0.50, 95% CI 0.32-0.77). For OS, only EBC (HR 0.52, 95% CI 0.39-0.69) and EC (HR 0.59, 95% CI 0.46-0.76) achieved statistically significant benefits. No significant difference was detected between EBC and EC on either endpoint. No between-study heterogeneity was detected (I2 = 0%). In the exploratory safety network, encorafenib plus cetuximab was the only encorafenib-based regimen associated with significantly fewer grade ≥ 3 adverse events than irinotecan plus cetuximab (odds ratio 0.67, 95% CI 0.47-0.96). CONCLUSION: These findings position encorafenib-based therapy, and encorafenib plus cetuximab in particular, as the reference standard for previously treated BRAF V600E-mutant mCRC, while underscoring that the incremental value of more intensive regimens must be weighed against tolerability and confirmed in adequately powered trials.

articles.title: Primary Endocrine Therapy vs Upfront Surgery for Older Women With Estrogen Receptor-Positive Breast Cancer: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract: IMPORTANCE: As the population of older women with breast cancer grows, an increasing number are considered for primary endocrine therapy (pET), yet clinicians lack a framework for identifying which patients are appropriate candidates, resulting in reliance on chronologic age and life expectancy rather than tumor biology. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate survival and variables associated with response duration for patients treated with pET. DATA SOURCES: PubMed, MEDLINE, Web of Science, and Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials were searched from inception through March 26, 2026. STUDY SELECTION: Randomized clinical trials (RCTs) and non-RCT (observational) cohorts comparing pET with surgery in operable, nonmetastatic, estrogen receptor (ER)-positive breast cancer. DATA EXTRACTION AND SYNTHESIS: Data were extracted independently by 2 reviewers per Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines. Hazard ratios (HRs) not directly reported were reconstructed from Kaplan-Meier curves. Randomized clinical trial-derived HRs for overall survival (OS) and breast cancer-specific survival (BCSS) were pooled using a random-effects model, given anticipated heterogeneity across trials spanning 5 decades and differing tumor biology criteria. Observational cohorts were analyzed descriptively, not pooled for comparative survival, given susceptibility to confounding by indication. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The main outcomes were OS and BCSS (RCTs) assessed using meta-analysis. Time to progression, salvage intervention rates, and variables associated with progression and mortality (observational cohorts) were assessed using descriptive analyses. RESULTS: Twenty-nine studies (6 RCTs and 23 observational cohorts; 22 821 patients; overall median [IQR] age, 83.1 [77.0-85.0] years) met the inclusion criteria. Patients from RCTs were generally younger (median [IQR] age, 77.0 [75.8-78.0] years) than those from the observational studies (median [IQR] age, 84.0 [81.5-86.0] years). Treatment with pET was not associated with a statistically significant OS difference vs surgery (HR, 1.14; 95% CI, 0.98-1.33), though the point estimate favored surgery. Median time to progression ranged from 19.7 months (range, 13.5-26.0 months) in tumor biology-unselected, tamoxifen-era cohorts to more than 50 months in ER-selected and aromatase inhibitor-treated cohorts. Tumor biology was consistently associated with progression risk. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: This systematic review and meta-analysis of more than 22 000 patients with ER-positive breast cancer found no statistically significant survival difference between pET and upfront surgery. Durable disease control under pET seemed to be concentrated in patients with favorable biology. These findings support a framework incorporating tumor biology and frailty, rather than age alone, to identify candidates for pET.

articles.title: Antibiotic Exposure and Treatment Outcomes in Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma and Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Systemic antibiotics may disrupt the gut and oral microbiome, potentially affecting anticancer treatment efficacy. Their prognostic relevance in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) and nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC), particularly during immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI)-based therapy or definitive chemoradiotherapy (CRT), remains uncertain. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated associations between systemic antibiotic exposure around treatment initiation and oncologic outcomes. METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and Scopus were searched from January 2015 to March 28, 2026. Eligible studies included patients with HNSCC or NPC receiving ICI, definitive CRT, or chemo-immunotherapy and reporting overall survival (OS), progression-free survival (PFS), or objective response rate (ORR). Random-effects models pooled hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for OS and PFS; ORR was synthesized descriptively. Risk of bias was assessed, as appropriate, using ROBINS-I, ROBINS-E, RoB 2, or the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. RESULTS: Eleven studies involving 6,293 patients were included; nine studies (4,507 patients) contributed to survival meta-analyses. Antibiotic exposure was associated with worse OS (HR 1.78, 95% CI 1.52-2.08) and PFS (HR 1.58, 95% CI 1.28-1.96). Associations were consistent in ICI-treated cohorts (OS HR 1.80, 95% CI 1.53-2.13; PFS HR 1.67, 95% CI 1.24-2.25) and CRT cohorts (OS HR 1.73, 95% CI 1.29-2.32; PFS HR 1.53, 95% CI 1.11-2.11). Heterogeneity was low-to-moderate for OS (I2=28.6%) and negligible for PFS (I2=0%). Leave-one-out analyses showed stable OS (HR range 1.76-1.86) and PFS estimates (1.58-1.63). Worse OS was observed for both 30-60-day pre-ICI exposure (HR 2.04, 95% CI 1.43-2.90) and concurrent/peri-treatment exposure (HR 1.74, 95% CI 1.49-2.04). ORR was descriptively lower in antibiotic-exposed patients. Most studies had serious/high risk of bias, primarily due to confounding by indication. CONCLUSIONS: Systemic antibiotic exposure around treatment initiation is associated with inferior survival and response in HNSCC and NPC. However, predominantly observational evidence and substantial confounding preclude causal inference. Prospective microbiome-informed studies are needed.

articles.title: Optimal duration of levetiracetam prophylaxis following supratentorial tumor resection: a multi-study analysis.
articles.abstract: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of short-course (≤ 9 days) versus extended-course levetiracetam (LEV) prophylaxis for preventing seizures in seizure-naïve patients following supratentorial tumor resection. A systematic review and meta-analysis were conducted across PubMed, Google Scholar, and the Cochrane Library. Eight studies encompassing nine distinct clinical cohorts (N = 385) were included. Studies were dichotomized into Short-Term (ST: ≤ 9 days) and Extended-Term (ET: > 9 days) groups. Pooled seizure incidence was analyzed using a random-effects model, and a multivariate meta-regression isolated drivers of seizure risk. A temporal crossover analysis mapped medication attrition against marginal prophylactic benefit. The ST group demonstrated a pooled seizure incidence of 2.4% (95% CI: 1.1%-4.6%), significantly below the 12% historical baseline. Conversely, ET cohorts exhibited higher, volatile rates (up to 34.7%), statistically indistinguishable from untreated late-onset benchmarks (20%). Meta-regression identified only treatment duration and tumor type as significant moderators of outcomes (p < 0.05); age, gender, and LEV dosage (1000-3000 mg) had no impact. Safety analysis revealed a day-14 "clinical pivot": early well-tolerated somatic effects transitioned to severe neuropsychiatric toxicity with extended therapy, driving high attrition rate. ST (≤ 9 days) LEV protocol provides maximal prophylactic efficacy with minimal toxicity. Extending prophylaxis beyond this window offers no incremental protection against late-onset seizures but subjects patients to an intolerable neuropsychiatric burden. While prospective control trials are necessary to establish definitive guidelines, our findings indicate that a short term LEV course may offer a highly favorable risk-benefit profile. Extending prophylaxis beyond this timeframe seems to offer minimal additional benefit while markedly elevating the risk of neu​ropsychiatric toxicity, thereby requiring prudent clinical evaluation.

articles.title: CEACAM5-Targeted Therapies in Solid Tumors: Biological Barriers and Next-Generation Precision Strategies.
articles.abstract: Carcinoembryonic antigen-related cell adhesion molecule 5 (CEACAM5) is an attractive therapeutic target because of its widespread overexpression in epithelial malignancies and its polarised, largely luminal expression in normal epithelium. Despite extensive clinical development, no CEACAM5-targeted drug has received regulatory approval. The Phase III CARMEN-LC03 trial highlighted the limitations of expression-based patient selection, as tusamitamab ravtansine failed to improve the ORR over docetaxel in patients with high CEACAM5 expression. This review argues that progress in CEACAM5-targeted therapy requires a shift from focusing solely on target expression to understanding the target's biological constraints. We first summarize the biological functions of CEACAM5 in tumor progression, then discuss the major biological barriers limiting therapeutic efficacy including GPI anchor-mediated slow internalization, soluble CEACAM5-mediated antigen sink effects, extensive glycosylation, antigen heterogeneity, and immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. Building on these biological barriers, we outline five priorities for next-generation development: targeting tumor-specific glycoforms, multi-antigen strategies, microenvironment remodeling, conditionally restricted delivery, and biomarker-guided clinical trial design. Future patient selection should integrate CEACAM5 expression with target biology and therapeutic modality compatibility to identify patients likely to benefit and reduce ineffective treatment.

articles.title: Nurse-Led Sepsis Scoring System for Adult Febrile Neutropenia: Protocol for a Two-Phase Clinical Prediction Model Study With Remote Patient Monitoring.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Adults with hematological malignancies who develop febrile neutropenia (FN) face elevated risks of sepsis, intensive care admission, and treatment interruptions. Early sepsis detection is challenging, as classical clinical signs are often attenuated or delayed in this population. Current risk stratification tools demonstrate limitations when applied to adults with FN. A tailored, nurse-led scoring system integrating clinical, laboratory, and physiological predictors may enhance early sepsis identification. OBJECTIVE: This 2-phase study aims to develop and internally validate a nurse-led sepsis risk score for adults with FN in phase I and to temporally validate its performance in phase II. The new score will be compared to the MASCC risk index, CISNE, NEWS2_ and qSOFA at FN onset . The secondary objectives include evaluating associations between risk groups and remote patient monitoring alerts within 24 hours of FN onset, interrater agreement, and bedside feasibility. METHODS: The study is being conducted in the hematology and bone marrow transplantation department of a tertiary care hospital in Bengaluru, India. Phase I uses a nested matched case-control design within a retrospective cohort of approximately 140 patients with FN. We will analyze clinical, laboratory, and physiological predictors measured at FN onset using multivariable conditional logistic regression, with internal validation via bootstrapping. In Phase II, which utilizes a prospective temporal validation cohort, bedside nurses will calculate the proposed score at FN onset alongside the MASCC, CISNE, NEWS2, and qSOFA scores A substudy will include additional nurses scoring independently to assess interrater agreement and feasibility. Two blinded reviewers will adjudicate phase I outcomes within 14 days of FN onset, while assessors blinded to all scores will adjudicate phase II outcomes within the same time frame. The primary outcome is sepsis within 14 days of FN onset. Phase II evaluates discrimination, calibration, and comparative diagnostic performance. RESULTS: We obtained ethics approval in April 2025, and the study was registered in June 2025 (CTRI/2025/06/088290). The initial phase I derivation was completed in November 2025, using sepsis within 14 days of FN onset as the primary outcome. A protocol amendment in September 2026 harmonized the outcome window to 14 days, prompting rederivation of the model and superseding the initial analysis. Phase II commenced in December 2025. As of September 2026, enrollment and data collection were ongoing, with study completion anticipated in December 2026. Main results are expected in 2027. CONCLUSIONS: This protocol evaluates an FN-specific, nurse-led sepsis score integrating clinical and laboratory predictors with contactless physiological measurements. We will examine remote patient monitoring alerts as secondary markers of clinical instability. Validation findings will establish the score's predictive performance and inform future implementation studies.

articles.title: A phase Ia first-in-human study of BPB-101, a novel trifunctional antibody targeting the GARP/TGF-β complex and PD-L1, in patients with locally advanced or metastatic solid tumors.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: BPB-101 is a first-in-class, humanized trifunctional bispecific IgG1 antibody targeting the GARP/TGF-β complex, active TGF-β, and PD-L1, with preclinical evidence of immunomodulatory and antitumor activity. This phase Ia study aimed to assess the safety, tolerability, pharmacology, and preliminary antitumor activity of BPB-101. METHODS: A modified accelerated titration design (6, 20, and 60 mg) was followed by a 3 + 3 escalation (200-1800 mg), with intravenous dosing every 3 weeks (Q3W). Eligible patients with advanced or metastatic solid tumors who had received prior standard systemic treatment were enrolled. The primary objectives were dose-limiting toxicity (DLT), maximum tolerated dose (MTD), and recommended phase II dose (RP2D). Secondary and exploratory objectives included pharmacokinetics (PK), pharmacodynamics (PD), immunogenicity, and preliminary antitumor activity. RESULTS: At the data cutoff of January 26, 2025, 19 patients with advanced tumors were enrolled. Treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs) occurred in 15 patients (78.9%), with the most common TRAEs being infusion-related reactions (26.3%), anemia (26.3%), and asthenia (21.1%). Grade ≥ 3 TRAEs were reported in two patients (10.5%), both of whom had anemia, with one patient each in the 400 mg and 800 mg groups. No DLTs or treatment-related deaths occurred, and the MTD was not reached. One patient in the 1800 mg cohort permanently discontinued treatment due to an immune-related TRAE (myalgia). BPB-101 exposure increased approximately dose-proportionately at doses ≥ 800 mg. Peripheral PD assessments showed high receptor occupancy (RO) and reductions in circulating TGF-β1 levels in the 1200 mg and 1800 mg cohorts. The 1200 mg and 1800 mg Q3W doses were selected as RP2Ds for further evaluation. Among 17 patients in the efficacy analysis set (EAS), one achieved confirmed immune partial response (iPR) and seven achieved immune stable disease (iSD). The overall immune objective response rate (iORR) was 5.9% (95% CI, 0.1-28.7), and the immune disease control rate (iDCR) was 47.1% (95% CI, 23.0-72.2). CONCLUSIONS: BPB-101 showed a manageable safety profile, peripheral PD activity, and preliminary antitumor activity, supporting further evaluation in expansion cohorts. TRIAL REGISTRATION: This study was registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05869240); part of the study was reported at ESMO ASIA 2025 as an oral presentation. Abstract No: 158O.

articles.title: A phase 1 study of 4'-thio-2'-deoxycytidine in patients with solid tumors.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: The DNA methyltransferase (DNMT) inhibitor 4'-thio-2'-deoxycytidine (TdCyd), a second-generation cytidine analog, demonstrated potent preclinical antitumor activity and favorable pharmacokinetics, which led us to explore its safety, efficacy and anti-tumor activity in patients with solid tumors. METHODS: Adult patients with advanced solid tumors received TdCyd orally on days 1-5 and 8-12 in 21-day cycles. Dose escalation proceeded according to design 4 of the Simon accelerated titration design, changing to a 3 + 3 dose escalation design in the event of dose-limiting toxicities. Blood samples were collected for circulating tumor cell (CTC) evaluation of p16 re-expression as a marker of TdCyd epigenetic modulation, and for pharmacokinetic analysis. RESULTS: Twenty-seven patients were enrolled. The maximum tolerated dose was not reached. The best response was prolonged stable disease (SD), with 3 patients on treatment for ≥ 6 cycles, and there was no dose-response relationship. An increase in the proportion of p16-expressing cytokeratin-positive (CK+) CTCs was detected in 71% (15 of 21) of patients evaluable for p16 response at every dose level in which patients were assessable for pharmacodynamic response; p16 re-expression in vimentin-positive CTCs was reported in 38% (6 of 16) of evaluable patients. Plasma levels of TdCyd metabolites were largely dose proportional and higher levels were detected in patients with higher incidence and severity of study drug-related adverse events. CONCLUSION: Prolonged SD and p16 re-expression at lower TdCyd dose levels suggest that longer exposures to low concentrations is worth exploring in future trials, including studies of TdCyd in therapeutic combinations.

articles.title: Tinostamustine-nivolumab therapy is associated with antigen-specific cellular and humoral immune responses in heavily pre-treated patients with advanced melanoma.
articles.abstract: ENIgMA is a phase IB trial (NCT03903458; SNCTP000003243) evaluating the safety and preliminary activity of the first-in-class alkylating deacetylase inhibitor tinostamustine in combination with nivolumab (3 mg/kg) in patients with predominantly immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI)-resistant, advanced melanoma. We conducted this longitudinal immune monitoring study in 15 of the 17 enrolled patients to characterize systemic immunologic changes associated with an immunomodulatory dose of tinostamustine. We have previously demonstrated that combination of tinostamustine with nivolumab was able to induce disease stabilization in 54% and confirmed partial responses in 23% of evaluable patients. Peripheral blood samples collected longitudinally during treatment were analysed by flow cytometry, serum antigen-specific IgG enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA), and intracellular cytokine staining following ex vivo peptide stimulation. Longitudinal flow cytometric analyses demonstrated dynamic changes in peripheral immune subsets, including T cells, natural killer (NK) cells and monocytes, suggesting ongoing immune engagement during tinostamustine-nivolumab therapy. In progressors, elevated baseline lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) levels significantly and inversely correlated with circulating T cell frequencies, indicating distinct immune profiles associated with poor clinical outcome. Antigen-specific adaptive immune responses were detectable despite extensive prior treatment and high tumour burden. CD4+ T cell responses, particularly TNFα-associated responses directed against melanoma-associated antigens, represented the dominant cellular immune activation pattern. Additionally, treatment related increases in melanoma-associated antigen-specific IgG responses were also observed in several patients. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that immunomodulatory doses of tinostamustine in combination with nivolumab are linked with preserved adaptive immune competence and detectable cellular and humoral immune activation in heavily pre-treated patients with advanced melanoma.

articles.title: Co-production of eENHANCE: a web platform to deliver personalised nutrition and exercise support to prevent cancer-related malnutrition and muscle loss.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Access to nutrition and exercise services for people with cancer-related malnutrition varies across health services. This study co-produced a personalised self-guided evidence-based nutrition and exercise web program and evaluated feasibility and acceptability within clinical practice. METHODS: A co-production approach was utilised following the four phases of Design Thinking in Healthcare. Phase 1 gathered user needs through interviews with consumers and health professionals, which were analysed using thematic analysis. Solutions were generated in Phase 2 to inform content and development of the platform. Phase 3 involved user acceptance testing. Feasibility testing in a clinical setting was undertaken in Phase 4. RESULTS: Phase 1: interviews with 14 health professionals (100% female, mean age 59.5 [range 25-57] years) and five people with cancer (100% female, mean age 53.5 [range 57-62] years) generated three themes: (1) patient characteristics, (2) features and functions of the web platform and (3) optimising practice. Phase 2: an 8-week evidence-based self-guided nutrition and exercise program (eENHANCE) was developed based on the interview findings and refined in Phase 3 testing. Phase 4: 20 people with cancer participated in feasibility testing of eENHANCE at a tertiary cancer centre, with high (86%) acceptability of the intervention, compliance with study outcome assessment (67-100%), while 30-100% accessed prescribed modules. CONCLUSIONS: eENHANCE is a unique self-guided personalised nutrition and exercise program for people at risk of cancer-related malnutrition and muscle loss. High acceptability and feasibility indicate there may be potential to expand access to self-guided programs for people recovering from cancer treatment; however, further work is required in people undergoing treatment and to identify the most appropriate target groups and the optimal strategies to reach them to improve intervention fidelity.

articles.title: Acceptability of a patient support and educational intervention for black breast cancer survivors.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Black women with breast cancer in the US experience worse survival and lower quality of life. Addressing information needs and providing emotional and social support may improve survivorship experiences. This study evaluated feasibility and acceptability of an intervention to support Black breast cancer patients. METHODS: English-speaking, Black, female breast cancer survivors diagnosed with stage I-III breast cancer within five years were invited to participate in a six-week group intervention (virtual or in-person). The intervention was adapted from the PAVING the Path to Wellness program based on a prior qualitative study. Primary endpoints were feasibility and acceptability. Exploratory endpoints included unmet information needs and well-being. Exit interviews with a subset of participants described experiences with, and benefits from, the intervention. RESULTS: 20 women with a mean age of 59.1 years (SD 8.2) and predominantly diagnosed at stage I (n = 11; 55%) participated. Most participants (n = 15; 88.3%) reported high levels of satisfaction and that the program provided new information relevant to their needs and helped motivate lifestyle changes. Nearly all participants (n = 15; 88.3%) expressed that it is important for other Black breast cancer survivors to receive a similar intervention. CONCLUSION: This study demonstrates proof of concept and provides insights into participant preferences. Broader-scale testing is needed to assess generalizability.
